gloss: A qualitative sociology study of campus free speech debates, using interviews with Northwestern undergraduates to examine how college students decide what counts as acceptable or unacceptable speech, including hate speech and speech restrictions, with implications for university speech policy.

title: Renewing and Recycling: The Formation of American Jewish Environmentalism in the 1970s and 1980s
gloss: A history thesis on how American Jews took part in the environmental movement of the 1960s-1980s, drawing on Jewish religious ethics, agricultural traditions and politics to shape faith-based environmentalism around issues like forests, vegetarianism, animal rights and alternative energy.

title: Going for Broke: Brokerage Behaviors in Organizations
gloss: Studies brokerage behavior in workplace social networks, comparing employees who connect coworkers with those who mediate between them, and how each orientation relates to team performance, team viability and coworker relationships, using national survey data on organizational teamwork.

title: Investigating the Effect of Intracortical Microstimulation (ICMS) in Brodmann's Area 2 Using Topographical Variational Autoencoding (VAE) Models
gloss: A computational neuroscience project modeling how electrical brain stimulation (intracortical microstimulation) of somatosensory cortex area 2 could restore proprioception, the sense of limb position and movement. It uses a self-organizing cortical map trained on natural arm movement to simulate stimulation effects for neural prosthetics.

title: Non-Specific Binding of Ni-NTA and Lipid Domains in Vesicles
gloss: Studies how lipid composition and lipid domains in synthetic vesicles used for targeted drug delivery affect specific and nonspecific binding to cancer cells, using Ni-NTA as a weak-binding model targeting molecule and flow cytometry to measure vesicle binding to Jurkat lymphocytes.

title: The Just World Hypothesis as a Psychological Defense in Individuals Living Under Acute vs. Chronic Terrorism Threats
gloss: A psychology survey study of how young adults living under acute versus chronic terrorism threats use belief in a just world as a coping defense, and how this relates to religiosity, comparing American and Israeli Jewish respondents.

title: Soviet Immigrants' Perspective on Mental Health and the Impact of Stigma
gloss: An ethnographic interview study of how immigrants from the former Soviet Union view mental health, examining the stigma around discussing it in the Soviet Union and how it shapes their attitudes toward Western practices like therapy and medication after immigrating to the United States.

title: Personality Traits and the Narration of Spiritual Experiences
gloss: A psychology study of how Big Five personality traits relate to the way mid-life adults narrate spiritual experiences, coding life-story accounts for themes of personal agency, the agency of spiritual beings, and the closeness of spiritual forces.

title: Spontaneous AMPA-Receptor Mediated Activity in Low Frequency Auditory Neurons
gloss: Studies spontaneous activity in low-frequency auditory brainstem neurons of birds, using patch clamp electrophysiology and drug blockers to test whether spontaneous synaptic currents depend on AMPA-type glutamate receptors, relating to how spontaneous firing shapes auditory circuit and frequency organization during development.

title: The Effect of Civilian Oversight on Police Accountability
gloss: Studies whether civilian oversight agencies improve police accountability in Chicago, using time-series analysis of police misconduct complaints and how often they are sustained before and after the creation of independent review bodies.

title: Let's Team Up! Understanding How People Form Teams Using Online Platforms
gloss: A social network analysis of how people form teams on online platforms, examining whether virtual team assembly leads people beyond their usual networks and which individual traits, such as prior relationships, shared gender or age, and popularity, affect who gets invited to join a team.

title: Standards of Care and Non-Binary Gender Affirming Surgeries: A Comparison Between Thailand and the US Online
gloss: Compares how gender-affirming surgeries are offered and advertised online to Western patients by Thai surgeons versus US surgeons, focusing on whether options for non-binary patients exist and how WPATH Standards of Care shaped binary-focused surgical markets in medical tourism.

title: Analysis of the Effect of COVID-19 on the Global Economies and Evaluation of Countries' Policy Responses
gloss: An economics study measuring how the COVID-19 pandemic affected GDP growth and unemployment across about 60 major economies, and evaluating how effective different countries' government policy responses were, using IMF, WHO, Oxford policy-tracker and Google mobility data.

title: Biphysical Forces on VSMC Phenotype
gloss: Cell biology research on how mechanical forces on blood vessel smooth muscle cells, applied using vasodilator and vasoconstrictor drugs, change chromatin, gene activity and cell fate, driving them toward bone-like cells in vascular calcification, the hardening of arteries, with the aim of finding new therapeutic targets.

title: Tariffs and Partisanship: Evaluating the Link Between Steel and Aluminum Tariffs and the Political Affiliation of American Firms
gloss: A political economy study of whether American firms' political party affiliation affects their success in obtaining exclusions from the 2018 Trump steel and aluminum tariffs from the Department of Commerce, examining partisanship in bureaucratic trade policy decisions.

title: Neonatal Euthanasia and Morality: What Ought We to Do with the Sick Child?
gloss: A bioethics and moral philosophy paper arguing that neonatal euthanasia of non-terminal newborns with life-altering conditions is morally impermissible, weighing views from disability advocates, philosophers and medical professionals on suffering, marginalization and end-of-life decisions.

title: The Impact of Online Communities on the Social Idenity of Sneakerheads
gloss: A study of how online sneaker communities shape the social identity of sneakerheads, using surveys and interviews with members of online forums to compare how sneaker fans gain knowledge, identify with sneaker culture, and form relationships online versus in person.

title: "[T]hats just how the game is": How Black and White Parents Think about Systemic Racial Structures
gloss: A study of how Black and White parents think about systemic racism, privilege and oppression, using thematic analysis of survey responses from parents imagining how their lives would differ if they were of the other race.

title: Response of Deciduous Forest Senescence Rate in Autumn to Environmental Changes
gloss: Uses satellite remote sensing and statistical modeling to study how quickly deciduous forests in the Northeastern United States change color and drop leaves in autumn, and how climate change, temperature, drought and heat stress affect this fall senescence rate.

title: Intergenerational Trauma, Gender Ideologies, and Resilience in Post-Apartheid South Africa: Implications for Mental Health During COVID-19
gloss: An ethnographic, interview-based study of how apartheid's legacy of intergenerational trauma and gender ideologies shape the mental health, coping and resilience of Black women in Soweto, South Africa, during the COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns.

title: Examining the Relationship Between Maternal Education and Pediatric Nutritional Health in Guatemala: Questioning the Role of Maternal Health Knowledge and Practices
gloss: Studies whether mothers' education affects child malnutrition and stunting in Guatemala through maternal health knowledge and practices, using Demographic and Health Survey data and regression analysis. Compares this explanation with wealth, ethnicity and regional inequality.

title: ChangEd Digital Marketing Strategy
gloss: A digital and social media marketing strategy for ChangEd, a student loan repayment app, built on survey research with students, graduates and parents. It recommends social media, website, SEO and search engine marketing campaigns to raise awareness and engagement, with budget and evaluation plans.

title: Inter-Peer Social Influence on Post-Graduation Opportunity: Exploring How Peer-to-Peer Social Networks can Influence the Trend Between the Freshmen on Track, Graduation, and College Enrollment Metrics in the Chicago Public High Schools
gloss: Studies how peer-to-peer social networks and social capital among students affect high school graduation and college enrollment in Chicago Public Schools, using surveys and interviews with Northwestern undergraduates who attended CPS, to suggest ways high schools can support students' post-graduation success.

title: Impact of High School Debate and Extracurricular Activity Funding on Future Academic Success
gloss: An economics study of whether high school funding for debate clubs and other extracurricular activities affects students' later academic success, using regression analysis of Illinois high schools' activity budgets against graduation and college enrollment rates.

title: Life on the Edge: The Impact of Status, Class, and Stigma on Patterns of Middle-Class Welfare Use
gloss: A sociology study of how status, economic class, and welfare stigma shape when middle-class households take up social assistance such as SNAP, energy assistance, and unemployment insurance, comparing periods of economic stability with the 2008 Great Recession and testing Weber's theory of status and class.

title: Heterogeneity of Virulence Gene Expression in Salmonella Typhimurium
gloss: Microbiology research on cell-to-cell variation in virulence gene expression in the pathogenic bacterium Salmonella Typhimurium, using fluorescent reporter genes and live-cell imaging of bacteria infecting macrophage immune cells to understand how pathogens control infection.

title: Perpetual Violence and Livable Resistance: Historicizing Louisiana's Toxically Fertile "Cancer Alley"
gloss: Studies environmental racism in Louisiana's petrochemical corridor known as "Cancer Alley," linking toxic pollution and cancer in Black communities to the legacy of plantation slavery. Uses St. John the Baptist and St. James parishes as case studies of health harm, community resistance, and calls for reparations and restorative justice.

title: "It's Me. I'm All You Have": An Examination of Authoritarian Electoral Propaganda Used by Augusto Pinochet and Donald Trump to Target Female Voters
gloss: A comparative political science study of how authoritarian leaders Augusto Pinochet and Donald Trump used electoral propaganda and fear tactics to appeal to conservative female voters, based on qualitative analysis of Chilean and American news archives, campaign commercials and social media.

title: Mathematical Modeling to Forecast U.S. Elections
gloss: Forecasting U.S. presidential, Senate and gubernatorial elections with an epidemiology-style differential equation model of how political party affiliation spreads across states, using polling data and simulated scenarios to make state-level predictions and compare their accuracy with popular forecasting sites.

title: Strangest Things: Nostalgia vs. Representation in "Kids on Bikes" Media
gloss: A film and media studies analysis of 1980s nostalgia media such as Stranger Things and It: Chapter Two, examining how these works balance nostalgia for the past with diverse representation of race, gender, and sexuality, and what that tension means for progressive politics in contemporary film and television.

title: Objects of Influence: Sacrality and Native American Material Culture Across Five Contexts
gloss: Anthropology research tracing sacred and ceremonial Native American objects through their life cycle of origin, acquisition, museum exhibition, repatriation and return, examining how museums, NAGPRA repatriation and cultural values shape the meaning and treatment of Indigenous material culture.

title: The Effect of Authorship and Typographic Errors on the Evaluation and Trust of Text
gloss: A psychology experiment on how an author's racial identity affects readers' trust in information from a text and their acceptance of false information. It compares readers' stated, subjective ratings of a White or Black author with an implicit, memory-based measure of trust and finds racial bias in the latter.

title: The Effect of Remote Learning on Secondary Ensemble-Based Music Education
gloss: A qualitative case study of how the COVID-19 shift to remote learning changed secondary school band, orchestra and choir teaching, based on interviews with Chicago-area public school music teachers about their adaptations and about what music education should teach.

title: The Role of Intrinsically Photosensitive Retinal Ganglion Cells - Perihabenular Region Circuit in Visual Threat Anticipation
gloss: A neuroscience study in mice of how light-sensing retinal cells (ipRGCs) and their connection to the perihabenular region of the brain help animals learn to anticipate visual threats, using melanopsin knockout mice, looming stimuli, chemogenetics and retinal circuit tracing.

title: Modernist Displays of 'Mestizo' Identity in Covarrubias' Mexican Street Scene
gloss: An art history study of a Miguel Covarrubias lithograph in the Block Museum's collection, examining how modernist art in post-revolutionary Mexico portrayed mestizo and Indigenous identity to build a national image for international audiences, and how such depictions relied on stereotypes.

title: Of Horses and Propensity: Exploring Close Counterfactuals
gloss: A cognitive psychology study of close counterfactuals, asking when people judge that an event almost happened. Using a horse race scenario, it tests how changes in an event's likelihood of success (propensity) shape people's judgments that the favored horse almost won.

title: Improving Ambient Stability of Nickel-Rich Lithium-Ion Battery Cathode Materials via Polymer and Graphene Coating
gloss: Materials science research on protecting nickel-rich lithium-ion battery cathodes from degradation by air, moisture and CO2, using a conformal graphene and ethylcellulose polymer coating to reduce lithium impurities and improve battery cycling performance for electric vehicles and grid energy storage.

title: Entering Dreamland: Infusing Signals into a Dream to Produce Awareness of Dreaming
gloss: Sleep and dream research on inducing lucid dreams, where sleepers know they are dreaming, using targeted memory reactivation: sound cues played during sleep, delivered remotely through a smartphone app. It also explores real-time communication with lucid dreamers.

title: "Friends With A Girl Like Me": Girlhood in Japanese Horror Video Games
gloss: A study of how independent, fan-translated Japanese horror video games depict adolescent girl (shojo) protagonists, analyzing girlhood, cuteness and the monstrous-feminine to show how gameplay and horror give young girls and players agency.

title: The Hindu Rashtra Meets Dar al-Islam: The Impact of Hindu Nationalism on India's Relations with Muslim-Majority Countries
gloss: A political science thesis on how Hindu nationalism under Narendra Modi affects India's foreign relations with Muslim-majority countries Iran, Turkey, and Malaysia, examining the intersection of religion and foreign policy and finding pragmatic interests outweigh religious tensions.

title: An Application of Bayesian Autologistic Actor Attribute Model s (ALAAM) to Study Social Networks and Their Influence on Human Behavior in Rural Kenya
gloss: Uses social network analysis and Bayesian autologistic actor attribute models (ALAAM) to study how social ties and community influence shape modern contraceptive use in a rural Kenyan community, with implications for family planning and public health policy in developing countries.

title: The Role of Demographics as a Determinant of Community Health Concerns
gloss: Analyzes community health survey data from Chicago and Little Rock to see how age, gender, location and other demographics shape which health issues residents see as most pressing, using principal component analysis and data visualization to inform community-tailored health policy and faith-based outreach.

title: Assessing Fertility Knowledge in Undergraduate Students
gloss: A survey study of undergraduate students' knowledge about fertility and age-related fertility decline, their plans to delay childbearing and anxieties about future fertility, and their preferred ways of learning about reproductive health, with attention to women planning medical careers.

title: Development and Assessment of a Hydrocephalus Shunt Flow Monitor
gloss: Development and testing of a flexible, wearable sensor that continuously monitors cerebrospinal fluid flow through hydrocephalus shunts, so that shunt blockage can be detected without brain scans or surgery. The work covers biomedical device design, materials, and sensor accuracy testing on a skin model.

title: How Does the Level of Cultural Similarities Between Refugees and Hosts Impact Social Integration?
gloss: A political science study of how cultural similarity between refugees and host societies affects social integration, comparing Syrian refugees in Jordan and Germany. It argues that host government refugee policy matters more than cultural overlap in shaping integration outcomes.

title: COVID-19 Vaccine Attitudes Among Native People
gloss: A survey study of COVID-19 vaccine hesitancy among Native American people, examining cultural, socioeconomic, political and psychological factors and testing which pro-vaccine messages are most persuasive, to help Native organizations design effective public health campaigns.

title: The Impact of SNAP and P- EBT in the Wake of COVID- 19
gloss: An economics study of how federal food assistance programs, SNAP (food stamps) and Pandemic-EBT, affected hunger, food insecurity and households' confidence in affording food during the COVID-19 pandemic, using Census Household Pulse Survey data and state participation data with regression and difference-in-differences analysis.

title: Entering the Black Box: Looking at Pretrial Risk Assessments' Machine Learning Process
gloss: Examines the transparency and consistency of pretrial recidivism risk assessment algorithms used in criminal justice, testing whether public records requests can reveal how tools like COMPAS and PSA work and comparing their risk scores for the same defendants. Addresses algorithmic accountability and fairness.

title: Radical Caring: A Qualitative Study on the Role of Frontline Workers in Eradicating Gender Violence in Asian American Communities
gloss: An anthropology study of how Asian American social workers and legal advocates in Chicago-area domestic violence agencies support survivors of gender-based violence, using feminist ethnography and interviews to examine their caring labor, Asian American communities, and violence prevention.

title: Energy Generation by Saltwater Motion on Metal Nanolayers
gloss: Renewable energy research on thin metal nanolayers made from Earth-abundant metals like iron and nickel that generate electricity from flowing saltwater, studying how they convert fluid motion into current, protecting them from saltwater degradation, and fabricating them on scalable substrates such as flexible plastic.

title: Constructing Convex Polyhedra by Applying Gaussian Curvature to Pentagons
gloss: A geometry and topology math research project extending Gauss's Theorema Egregium and Gaussian curvature to polyhedral surfaces, studying how pentagons can be folded and glued with a companion pentagon to form convex polyhedra, using proofs, Mathematica computations, and paper models.

title: Washed Away: Come Towards for String Quartet Description
gloss: An original contemporary classical composition for string quartet, written during the COVID-19 pandemic, exploring tension, release and relaxation through extended string techniques like harmonics, trills and bow contrasts. Composed and recorded in collaboration with the Spektral Quartet through the Bienen School of Music's Institute for New Music.

title: My Mother Fled to the Submerged Palace Description
gloss: An animated short film adapting the Thai folktale The Golden Goby Fish to modern-day Bangkok, told without dialogue, exploring grief and acceptance and presenting Thai culture as contemporary rather than rooted in the past.

title: Dam-Displaced Populations Experience Significantly Higher Household Water Insecuirty, Food Insecurity, Depression, and Domestic Violence due to Construction of the Thwake Multipurpose Dam in Makueni County, Kenya
gloss: A global health study of how displacement by construction of the Thwake Multipurpose Dam in Kenya affects women's well-being, using survey scales to compare household water insecurity, food insecurity, depression, and domestic violence between dam-displaced and other households.

title: A Flower Explodes (Staged Reading) Description and Artist Statement
gloss: An original play, presented as a staged reading in Mandarin and Shanghai and regional dialects, about three generations of Chinese women in a Shanghai longtang neighborhood from 1957 to 1966. It explores feminism, mother-daughter relationships, migration, collectivism and forgotten history in twentieth-century China.

title: These Days (Animated Short Film) Description and Artist Statement
gloss: A 2D-animated short film, written, illustrated and animated by the student, about depression, anxiety and the sameness of daily routine during a period of pandemic stagnation. It reflects on the beauty and sadness found in mundane everyday life.

title: Maternal and Paternal Depression Symptoms During the NICU Stay, Transition Home, and First 30 days
gloss: A longitudinal study of postpartum depression symptoms in mothers and fathers of infants in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), tracking how parental mental health changes from NICU admission through discharge and the first month home, and whether in-hospital depression screening predicts later depression.

title: A Bridge to the Moon (Musical Theater Film) Description and Artist Statement
gloss: An original musical theater film written, composed and performed by students during COVID-19, telling a folk-tale about three grieving siblings on a mythical island facing an environmental crisis. The project explores grief, childhood dreams and community care while making live theater safely beyond Zoom.

title: Identifying Deficiencies in Food Allergy Awareness and Accommodation on College Campuses
gloss: A survey study of U.S. college students with food allergies, examining how well universities and campus dining halls recognize and accommodate food allergies, including allergic reactions in dining halls, food labeling, staff training, and access to emergency epinephrine.

title: Vimentin is a Requirement for Complete Closure of the Ductus Arteriosus
gloss: Developmental cardiovascular biology research in mice on how the ductus arteriosus closes after birth, testing whether the intermediate filament protein vimentin is needed for closure and how it relates to patent ductus arteriosus, a congenital heart defect, and Notch signaling.

title: You Had to Be There: Jewish Humor in the Holocaust as a Complex Form of Resistance
gloss: A history project on how Jews used humor (jokes, performances and art) during the Holocaust in ghettos, hiding and concentration camps as a form of resistance and survival, drawing on survivor interviews and archival materials analyzed through psychology, sociology and the history of genocide resistance.

title: Up Close & Personal: The Effects of Psychological Distance on Moral Judgments
gloss: A psychology experiment testing how psychological distance, framed through Construal Level Theory, shapes moral judgments in trolley-problem-style dilemmas, comparing abstract versus concrete descriptions of whether sacrificing one life to save others is acceptable.

title: Black Parenting Experiences & Perceived Parental Health Impacts
gloss: An interview study of Black parents in the Chicago area exploring how structural racism, discrimination, and fears for their children's futures affect parents' mental, emotional, and physical health, along with the coping strategies and joys of parenting that offset that stress.

title: American Jewish Identity in Conversation with Zionism, Antisemitism, and Social Justice
gloss: An interview-based sociology study of progressive American Jewish college students at Northwestern and how they reconcile Jewish identity and support for Israel/Zionism with left-leaning social justice spaces, campus Israel/Palestine tensions, and experiences of antisemitism.

title: Feasibility and Acceptability of Fit2ThriveMB: A Technology-Based Intervention for Patients with Metastatic Breast Cancer
gloss: Tests whether a mobile health app with Fitbit tracking and coaching calls is feasible and acceptable for increasing physical activity in patients with metastatic breast cancer, using a randomized pilot study with participant surveys and interviews.

title: Application of Ovarian Anatomy Nomenclature to Classify and Quantify Follicles in the Rhesus Macaque Ovary
gloss: Develops a standardized method for classifying ovarian follicles by developmental stage and counting them in rhesus macaque ovary tissue, using NIH ovarian anatomy nomenclature. Compares follicle counts in young and old monkeys to study reproductive aging and fertility in non-human primates.

title: Do You Have a Type or Just a Lack of Choice? Measuring the Stability of Physical Attraction Types across Environments
gloss: A psychology survey study of college students examining whether people's physical attraction 'types' are stable, and how the diversity of their high school and college environments shapes how consistent their attraction preferences are.

title: Establishing A Quantitative Proteostasis Probe for Neuronal Signaling Receptor Trafficking Upon Protein Aggregation
gloss: Develops a fluorescent molecular probe that measures clathrin-mediated endocytosis in cells as a readout of chaperone availability when misfolded proteins aggregate, relevant to neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's and to screening potential therapeutic drugs.

title: Identifying the Role of Niche Signaling in Hofstenia Miamia Regeneration
gloss: Developmental biology research on whole-body regeneration in the acoel worm Hofstenia miamia, using gene silencing to identify stem cell niche signaling pathways, such as TGF-beta homologs, that control how pluripotent stem cells (neoblasts) regenerate head and tail tissue after amputation.

title: Monstrous Masculinities and the Portrayal of Adolescent Development in the Twilight Saga
gloss: A literary analysis of masculinity in the Twilight Saga, reading Midnight Sun through psychoanalytic theory and Gothic fiction to examine how its vampire and werewolf heroes portray adolescent development and offer alternatives to toxic, patriarchal masculinity in Young Adult literature.

title: Novel Mechanisms in Nuclear Receptor Gene Regulation
gloss: Computational drug discovery study of how small molecules might regulate the orphan nuclear receptor Nurr1, linked to Parkinson's disease, by binding its coactivator NCoA1. Uses in silico high-throughput screening and Rosetta modeling to identify candidate lipid ligands and their binding poses.

title: How Remote Work Will Reshape Our Cities: Exploring the Heterogeneity in Pandemic-Era Urban Housing Price Changes
gloss: An economics study of how pandemic-era remote work changed urban housing demand, using zip-code Census demographics and Zillow housing prices to examine which kinds of residents, such as young professionals, left cities and what that means for urban demographics and businesses.

title: Connecting Conductivity with Surface Nanostructure for a Clean Energy Catalyst
gloss: Materials science study of cerium oxide (ceria) as a catalyst for clean energy devices such as fuel cells, testing whether the orientation of its surface nanostructure affects reaction kinetics. Thin ceria films with different surface orientations are measured using electrical conductivity relaxation to compare reaction rates.

title: Evaluating the Long-Term Effects of Hepatitis-B Infection on the Gut Microbiome of Captive Chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes)
gloss: Compares the gut microbiome of captive chimpanzees with and without hepatitis B virus infection, using DNA sequencing and metabolomics of fecal samples to study how a chronic viral liver infection relates to gut bacteria, immunity and microbial diversity in a primate model for human health.

title: After Wrongdoing: Exploring the Relationship Between Moral Threat, Withdrawl, and Repair
gloss: A social psychology experiment on how guilt and shame shape people's responses after they believe they have wronged someone, testing whether these moral emotions lead to repairing the relationship or withdrawing from the person harmed.

title: The Power of Social Justice Movements on College Campuses: Perceptions From Past and Present Student-Led Campus Movements at Northwestern University
gloss: A study of student-led social justice activism at Northwestern University, including the Community Not Cops police abolition movement, using newspaper content analysis and interviews to examine how students, faculty and administrators have perceived campus activism over time.

title: Sex Differences in Autism: A Prosodic Analysis
gloss: Studies sex differences in speech prosody (pitch, intonation, rhythm) among males and females with autism spectrum disorder compared to controls, using acoustic analysis of recorded storytelling, and how prosody relates to social communication and pragmatic language difficulties.

title: I Speak, Therefore I Am: An Exploration of the Relationship Between World Language Study and Black Student Identity
gloss: An interview study of how Black American college students perceive the relationship between their racial identity and studying world languages, covering experiences of community, marginalization, representation and instructor diversity in foreign language classrooms, with implications for culturally responsive language teaching.

title: Religiosity, Voter Turnout, and Congressional Representation of Black Americans
gloss: A political science study of how church and religion shape voter turnout among Black Americans, combining interviews with Chicago-area residents and analysis of survey data and House roll call votes to examine whether higher Black turnout leads to better congressional representation.

title: "I Wasn't Going to Wear No Shorts": Baseball and the Ideals of Mid-Twentieth Century Black Womanhood
gloss: A history thesis on the first women to play professional baseball with men in the Negro Leagues, examining how these Black women athletes challenged gender and racial expectations of Black womanhood in the Jim Crow era United States.

title: The Impact of Racial Identification on Asian Americans' Intergroup Empathy
gloss: A social psychology study of how Asian Americans' racial identification as Asian, American, or a person of color shapes their empathy toward White and Black people facing unfair treatment, using an online survey experiment and examining perceived discrimination as an explanation.

title: Exploring the Relationship between Adult Attachment Styles and One's Proclivity towards Supporting or Not Supporting One's Partner in a Romantic Relationship
gloss: A social psychology study of romantic relationships examining how adult attachment styles, especially avoidant attachment, relate to supporting versus controlling a partner's personal growth (the Michelangelo and Pygmalion phenomena), and whether Machiavellianism helps explain the link.

title: Teaching the Apocalypse: Emotional Management in Climate Change Education
gloss: A sociology study of how college instructors manage students' emotions, such as climate anxiety, when teaching about climate change, and how students cope with it. It draws on interviews and classroom observations of environmental studies courses at Northwestern, using theories of emotional labor.

title: Strongly Luminescent Hybrid Lead Halides with a Symmetric Triamine
gloss: Synthesis and characterization of new hybrid organic-inorganic lead halide materials, related to perovskites, built with a symmetric triamine molecule. The project studies their crystal structures and strong light emission (photoluminescence) for use in optoelectronic devices such as LEDs and solar cells.

title: Deceptively Progressive: Are Evanston's Reparations in Name Only?
gloss: A thesis evaluating Evanston, Illinois's local reparations program for Black residents, the first in the U.S., using city council records, community voices, newspapers and U.N.-based criteria to ask whether its housing program truly repairs the harms Black Evanstonians identify.

title: With Great Power Comes Great Responsibility: Voting Power and Self-Interest
gloss: A political science experiment, using an economic game and a policy study, testing whether having more voting power (pivotality) makes people vote more or less in their own self-interest, with implications for voting rights restrictions and epistocracy.

title: Social Media Usage and Anxiety
gloss: A survey study of how social media use affects anxiety and mental health in young adults, comparing undergraduates in the United States and China and testing whether sleep quality and digital stress mediate the relationship.

title: TECtalks: A Podcast Series Focused on Educating Listeners in Technology, Ethics, and Climate
gloss: An educational podcast series on the environmental impact of everyday technology, such as data center energy and water use and battery mineral mining. It draws on expert interviews and research to explore individual and collective actions for addressing technology's role in climate change and environmental injustice.

title: Media Rhetoric Surrounding Black Women in Rap and Sports: Exploring Cognitive Dissonance in People's Viewing of Social Topics
gloss: A study of racist and sexist media treatment of Black women in rap music and sports, using Twitter posts and Qualtrics surveys to examine double standards and cognitive dissonance in how the public judges Black female rappers and athletes compared with other groups.

title: "One American Family": Can Familial Relationships Decrease Partisan Hate and Increase Out-Party Respect?
gloss: A social psychology experiment on political polarization testing whether framing partisans as family members reduces out-party hate and increases respect for the opposing party. Democrats watched a staged political argument framed as between relatives or co-workers, then rated warmth toward the arguers and typical voters of each party.

title: GoodAsNU: A Community-Based Approach to Reducing E-Waste Through Electronics Self-Repair
gloss: Studies electronic waste and consumer electronics self-repair at Northwestern, using interviews with students, staff and faculty plus hands-on phone and laptop repairs to understand repair barriers and planned obsolescence, informing a community repair workshop to promote a culture of repair.

title: Can Actual Administration of Prescribed Acetaminophen Be Used as a Quality Improvement Measure?
gloss: A quality improvement study using retrospective electronic medical record data to examine how often acetaminophen is prescribed and given after surgery at a university hospital, comparing prescribing across surgeons and surgical services as an opioid-sparing pain management strategy.

title: Talking About Race in the Sociocultural Moment: Emerging Adults' Critical Consciousness and Racial Identity in Context
gloss: A psychology study of how white and BIPOC college students understand their racial identity and societal inequity through critical consciousness, analyzing their accounts of race-related conversations around the 2020 election to compare critical reflection, activism, and political efficacy across racial groups.

title: Assessing the Functional Impact of Phosphorylation on the Neurological Receptor mGluR2
gloss: Molecular neuroscience project on how phosphorylation of the brain glutamate receptor mGluR2 controls its signaling sensitivity, using phosphorylation-mimicking and phosphorylation-blocking receptor mutants expressed in human cells and compared through cell imaging.

title: The Effect of Outside Recommendations on Choosing Romantic Prospects
gloss: A social psychology survey experiment on online dating and partner selection, testing whether recommendations from a close friend or a dating app's matching algorithm change how young single adults rate dating profiles for attraction and ideal partner traits.

title: Music Education in the Pandemic
gloss: Qualitative interview study of how the COVID-19 shift to online learning affected AMASE, a Northwestern program offering free music lessons to local students with special needs and disabilities, drawing on the experiences of student teachers, students and families.

title: Investigating the Role of Alix in the Spread of Amyloid Pathology in APP Knock-In Mouse Models
gloss: Alzheimer's disease neuroscience research using mouse models to test whether the vesicle-release protein Alix drives the spread of amyloid-beta pathology in the brain. Uses Alix knockout transgenic mice, brain tissue staining, and ELISA to measure amyloid burden as a possible therapeutic target.

title: Investigation of Whether Environmental Context Affects the Antimicrobial Efficacy of Copper-Coated Surfaces
gloss: Tests whether environmental conditions such as humidity and the liquid medium carrying bacteria (saline or artificial saliva) change how well copper-coated surfaces kill bacteria, simulating high-touch hospital surfaces to inform the use of antimicrobial copper materials in healthcare and residential settings.

title: Educational Assortative Mating and Income Inequality in Brazil
gloss: An economics study of how educational assortative mating, the tendency of people with similar education to marry each other, affects household income inequality in Brazil, using regression analysis to examine the role of rising female education levels in a middle-income country context.

title: I Know You Are But What Am I: Presentation and Labelling within Sexual Identity
gloss: A sociology interview study of how queer college students label and present their sexual and gender identities, examining how they choose between umbrella and specific identity terms depending on social context and how social norms shape the labels they share with others.

title: Temporal Strain Data Reconstruction from Echocardiographic Strain Graphs
gloss: Develops an automated image-processing method to recover numerical heart muscle strain time-series data from saved images of echocardiography strain graphs, so archived cardiac imaging studies can be used for statistical and artificial intelligence analysis of heart disease.

title: Intelligent Coaching Systems: Understanding One-to-Many Coaching for Ill-Structured Problem Solving
gloss: A human-computer interaction study of how one coach guides many novices through open-ended problems such as product development in a university incubator, using video analysis to build a task model of coaching strategies and draw design implications for intelligent coaching and educational support systems.

title: Learning Loss and COVID-19: Pandemic Schooling Mode for U.S. Public Schools and Student Test Scores
gloss: An economics study of COVID-19 learning loss, examining how pandemic schooling mode (in-person, hybrid, or remote instruction) in U.S. public school districts during 2020-21 affected student standardized test scores in math, English, and the SAT.

title: Targeted: A Short Film In-Progress Exploring Modern-Day Surveillance Capitalism
gloss: A short film script exploring surveillance capitalism, the commodification of personal behavioral data for profit, as an everyday control tactic. The project draws on research into surveillance capitalism and into how films communicate complex social issues to wide audiences, aiming to spark public dialogue.

title: Examining the Relationship Between Parent Stress and Infant Development
gloss: Studies how parental stress relates to developmental delays in premature infants, using parent questionnaires to compare mothers' stress levels with infants' developmental screening scores at 12 months, including whether infants with a medical diagnosis are linked to higher parent stress.

title: Did the Cournot Paradox Apply to the Merger of American Airlines & US Airways?
gloss: An economics study of the 2013 American Airlines and US Airways merger, using regression analysis of route-level passenger data from 2012 to 2019 to test whether the Cournot merger paradox held, with non-merging airlines capturing market share, and what this means for antitrust policy on airline mergers.

title: 'When Did the Representation Become More Traumatic than the Reality?' Black Trauma Porn and the Question of Black Representation in Film
gloss: A critical analysis of the term "Black trauma porn" and Black representation in American film and television, arguing that such media is better understood as a subgenre of Black horror, drawing on film spectatorship, the history of race in Hollywood, and a case study of the series Them.

title: The Mental Health of Older Gender Minorities: A Review of the Literature
gloss: A literature review on the mental health of transgender and gender minority adults aged 50 and older, examining depression, suicidality, risk and protective factors, barriers to treatment, and mental health disparities compared with the general population.

title: Mapping Personality Across the United States
gloss: Maps personality traits across the contiguous United States using large-scale online personality survey data and R, and builds a depression scale from survey items, validating it against national public health depression data at the county level to explore regional psychological and mental health patterns.

title: Gendered Messages in The Handmaid's Tale: Offred's Evolution, 1985 – 2017
gloss: A feminist media studies comparison of gender representation across The Handmaid's Tale's 1985 novel, 1990 film adaptation, and 2017 TV series, examining how the narrative and visual portrayal of Offred changed in each version and how audiences and critics received them.

title: The Impact of Wage Spending on Team Performance in Soccer: Evidence From the Premier League
gloss: A sports economics study of whether player wage spending improves soccer team performance in the English Premier League, using regression models to test the effects of total payroll, wage inequality within teams, and the playing time of superstar players.

title: Clock Regulation of Glucose Metabolism During Diabetes
gloss: Studies how the circadian clock in skeletal muscle regulates glucose metabolism and insulin sensitivity in type 2 diabetes, using mice lacking the clock gene Bmal1 in muscle and fed a high-fat diet to model diet-induced obesity.

title: Screening for Contributing Factors and Countermeasures to Spaceflight-Induced Changes to the Gut Microbiome Through Bioinformatical Analysis Using STARMAPs
gloss: A bioinformatics study of how spaceflight changes the gut microbiome, comparing data from mice flown on the International Space Station with other datasets to find Earth-based stressors that cause similar shifts and dietary supplements, such as prebiotics and probiotics, that could counteract them.

title: Parenting Education for High School Students: An Examination of the ParentABLE Curriculum Implementation in Illinois
gloss: An evaluation of ParentABLE, a parenting education curriculum piloted in Illinois public high schools, using pre- and post-tests to measure changes in students' knowledge of child development and positive parenting, and whether student demographics or school characteristics predict learning gains.

title: Imaging Hydrated Harbor Seal Whiskers to Better Understand Perception
gloss: Develops methods for CT scanning harbor seal whiskers while they stay hydrated, to measure the 3D whisker shape that lets seals sense water movements and catch prey. Tests how whiskers change as they dry out and uses iodine contrast to tell whiskers apart from water.

title: Crises and Democracy: Freedom of the Press as a Measure of Democratic Change During the Covid-19 Pandemic
gloss: A comparative political science study of how the Covid-19 pandemic affected democracy and democratic backsliding, using press freedom as the measure. Case studies of New Zealand, Brazil, Hungary and the Philippines examine whether governments adopt more illiberal policies during crises.

title: Simon Pokagon: Remapping and Visualizing Potawatomi Presence at the 1893 World's Fair
gloss: An Indigenous literatures study of Potawatomi author Simon Pokagon at the 1893 Chicago World's Fair, analyzing his writings, Indigenous and settler maps of Chicago-area Potawatomi homelands, and images of Pokagon to examine Native presence, space, and racial and commercial gazes in the late 19th century.

title: Exploring Psychosocial Burdens of Diabetes in Pregnancy and the Role of TechnologyBased Support
gloss: Qualitative interview study of the emotional and psychological burdens of gestational and type 2 diabetes during pregnancy among low-income patients, and how a smartphone app supporting diabetes self-management helped ease those burdens.

title: The INS Shooting of Margarito Rosendo Padilla: Latina/o Immigration Activism During Chicago's Chicano Movement, 1972-1974
gloss: A history of Latina/o immigrant rights activism in Chicago during the Chicano Movement, tracing how the 1972 INS shooting of an immigrant in Pilsen sparked community organizing against immigration enforcement violence. Draws on newspapers, archives and oral histories to examine citizenship, belonging and racialization.

title: Tuning Gas Diffusion Electrode Construction to Mitigate Flooding and Degradation Processes for Electrochemical CO Reduction
gloss: Chemical engineering research on gas diffusion electrodes for electrochemical CO2 reduction, a technology for converting carbon dioxide into fuels and chemicals with renewable electricity. The project tests how electrode construction affects flooding, loss of hydrophobicity and degradation over time.

title: Attempts to Augment Refutation Text Benefits with Visualizations
gloss: Psychology experiments testing whether adding data visualizations to refutation texts helps correct people's misconceptions about climate change, measuring changes in participants' knowledge and beliefs. The work studies science misinformation, belief revision and learning from text and graphics.

title: Acquisition of Resistant Bacteria: Maternal Colonization with ESBL Enterobacteriaceae
gloss: Studies how antibiotic-resistant ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae bacteria, such as E. coli, pass from parents to newborns around birth and colonize the infant gut microbiome, using swabs and stool samples from Chicago-area hospitals that are cultured and characterized with PCR and DNA sequencing.

title: CEO Employment History at Hiring Firm and Hiring Firm Performance, 1990-2021
gloss: An empirical corporate finance study of whether hiring internal versus external CEOs affects the performance of publicly traded S&P 1500 firms, examining CEO succession, board hiring decisions, and how effects differ by firm size.

title: The Effect of Building Materials on Families' Spatial Conversations During a Playful Construction Activity
gloss: A developmental psychology study of how the number of building materials affects parents' and children's spatial language and conversations during a playful family construction activity, building a ramp from recyclables over Zoom, and what this means for supporting children's spatial skill development.

title: The Impact of Youth Onset Type 2 Diabetes on Postoperative Wound Healing Complications
gloss: Studies whether youth-onset type 2 diabetes raises the risk of postoperative complications such as surgical site infections and poor wound healing in young adults, using national surgical outcomes database records to compare diabetic and non-diabetic patients.

title: A Study of the Instructed Societal Perspective as a Mitigator of Social Desirability Bias
gloss: A social psychology experiment testing whether asking people how society views a group, rather than their personal view, reduces social desirability bias in reported attitudes. It compares personal and societal ratings of Black Americans with implicit racial bias measures.

title: Impact of Educators on Marginalized Students' Academic Outcomes
gloss: Educational psychology review of how teachers' beliefs about students' backgrounds affect motivation, persistence and achievement among marginalized, low-income students, focusing on strengths-based views of cultural identity rather than deficit-based framing.

title: Discovering Research Through the Voices of Black Girls
gloss: A reflection on undergraduate research experience in qualitative psychology studies of adolescent Black girls' racial and gender identities, including interview analysis and an afterschool identity program. It explores researcher positionality, critical self-reflection, and resisting oppression in research.

title: Amyloid-Beta Oligomers in the Embryonic Chick Retina: Understanding the Role of These Toxic Proteins in the Development of the Central Nervous System
gloss: Developmental neuroscience research on the normal role of amyloid-beta oligomers, proteins linked to Alzheimer's disease, in forming the retina and central nervous system, using chick embryos to test whether blocking them disrupts retinal development and horizontal cells.

title: JoeVincent So: Blue-Collar Fighter, White-Collar Preacher
gloss: A journalistic feature profile of a Filipino mixed martial artist working in Qatar, following his combat sports ambitions, faith, and family pressures to highlight the struggles and perseverance of expatriate workers in a country with little MMA infrastructure.

title: Positivity Resonance in Friendships, Friendship Satisfaction, and Loneliness: Evidence from a Dyadic Interaction Study
gloss: A psychology study of shared positive emotions (positivity resonance) between adolescent and young adult friends during recorded conversations, examining how these moments relate to friendship satisfaction and loneliness.

title: Bringing Home Spot: Domestication and Human-Dog Relationships Across the Ancient Americas
gloss: A literature-based anthropology project on dog domestication in the ancient Americas, combining zooarchaeological and genetic research with Indigenous North American and Mesoamerican cultural views of wolves and dogs to examine how social and emotional human-canid bonds shaped domestication.

title: Performance Studies: Queer Expressions of Love & Loss
gloss: Archival and museum research on how queer artists of color express love and loss across music, sculpture and digital media, and how racial dynamics shape which artists' histories get preserved in archives. Part of a performance studies research assistantship.

title: The Effect of Hedonic vs. Eudaimonic Employee Benefits on Work Engagement and WellBeing
gloss: A psychology experiment comparing hedonic employee benefits (pleasure and enjoyment, like free meals or massages) with eudaimonic benefits (purpose and growth, like volunteering or professional development) and their effects on employee work engagement and well-being, motivated by worker retention during the Great Resignation.

title: Under Arabo-Islamic Eyes: Indigeneity and Digital Language Practices in Morocco
gloss: A media studies case study of how Amazigh (Indigenous) people in Morocco use Tamazight in self-produced online COVID-19 health videos, examining digital alternative media as a grassroots response to Arab-Islamic nation-building, state language policy, and Indigenous language erasure.

title: "Not Good For Business": A Postcolonial Reading Of Marco Through The Lens Of Mimicry (In Exhibition Only- Not for Judging)
gloss: A postcolonial film analysis of the short film Marco, using Homi Bhabha's concept of mimicry to examine how queer Arab identity, language and sexuality are portrayed in post-Arab Spring and neo-colonial contexts, and what queer Arab cinema says about authenticity.

title: Does One Size (Model) Fit All?: Effects of Body Size on Clothing Attitudes
gloss: A psychology experiment on how model body size in fashion advertising affects women's attitudes, comparing thin versus ultra-thin models and measuring evaluations of the brand, the models' appearance, and the clothing's appeal and perceived value, in the context of size-inclusive advertising and body image.

title: Gesture as a Compensatory Mechanism During Narrative Retell in Former Late Talkers
gloss: A child language development study comparing how preschool children who were late talkers and typically developing children use hand gestures while retelling a story, testing whether gesture compensates for language delay in narrative skills.

title: CRISPRi Mediated Mutation of Pseudomonas Aeruginosa for Targeting Genes Involved with Biofilm Formation
gloss: Uses CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) gene repression in the antibiotic-resistant pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa to suppress genes involved in biofilm formation, then measures effects on biofilm growth, as part of a search for new therapeutics against drug-resistant bacterial infections.

title: Efficacy of Bioactive Glass in Healing Diabetic Wounds
gloss: Biomaterials project developing a copper-containing bioactive glass ointment to speed healing of chronic diabetic wounds, using the glass's ability to promote new blood vessel growth and copper's antibacterial effects as a lower-cost alternative to skin grafts and cell-based therapies.

title: Performance-Based Anxiety in High-Achieving Students
gloss: An interview study of how academic performance pressure and anxiety affect the mental health, social relationships, and academic wellbeing of high-achieving college students, drawing on interviews with Northwestern undergraduates about achievement identity, family and peer expectations, and access to mental health support.

title: Acute Caloric Restriction Attenuates the Age-Associated Loss of Ovarian Follicle Number in a Population of Peri-Menopausal Rhesus Macaques
gloss: Studies whether caloric restriction slows ovarian aging in young and old rhesus macaques, counting ovarian follicles in stained tissue sections to assess the ovarian reserve. Relates diet to female fertility, menopause and reproductive longevity in a non-human primate model.

title: Universal Screening & Intervention for Formula Need in Pediatric Primary Care Clinics During the COVID-19 Pandemic (In Exhibition Only- Not for Judging)
gloss: Evaluates a program that screens families at pediatric primary care clinics for infant formula and diaper need during the COVID-19 pandemic, connecting them to social workers, public benefits like WIC and SNAP, and onsite supply distribution to address child food insecurity.

title: Understanding Trans- and Gender Nonbinary Experiences with Being Misgendered and Attributional Claims
gloss: A psychology study of how transgender and nonbinary adults experience being misgendered by strangers and people close to them, using surveys and interviews to examine how they explain why it happened (causal attribution) alongside depression, anxiety, identity strength and felt stigma.

title: Mapping "Impossibilities": Queerness and Anti-Colonial Struggle in Palestine (In Exhibition Only- Not for Judging)
gloss: A review paper on queer politics and the Palestinian anti-colonial struggle, bringing academic literature and activists' writings into conversation on intersectionality, homonationalism, and pinkwashing, and critiquing Western queer theory and liberal rights-based approaches to sexuality in South-West Asia and North Africa.

title: Air Quality Benefits and Tradeoffs from 30% Light-Duty Vehicle Electrification over the Midwest-Great Lakes Region
gloss: Uses air quality and weather modeling to simulate how replacing 30% of gasoline cars with electric vehicles in the Midwest and Great Lakes region would change air pollution, accounting for power plant emissions from charging, and estimates the resulting public health impacts.

title: Impact of Regulatory Gene Expression on Salmonella Physiology
gloss: Microbiology research on how expression levels of the regulatory gene ssrB affect Salmonella bacteria, using engineered plasmids to compare bacterial growth under different nutrient conditions and the ability to invade mammalian host cells, exploring tradeoffs in pathogen infection.

title: Dual Language Input from Adults and Other Children in Two Communities
gloss: Studies how much of each language bilingual infants hear from adults versus other children, using daylong home audio recordings of Spanish-speaking immigrant families in the US and Quechua-Spanish families in Bolivia. It examines how speaker, addressee and community shape early dual language exposure.

title: Extraction of a Robotic Measure of Joint Stiffness in Individuals Post Hemiparetic Stroke for Comparison with a Shear Wave Ultrasound Elastography Measure
gloss: Measures elbow joint stiffness in stroke survivors with arm impairment using a robotic device, producing a gold-standard reference for validating shear wave ultrasound elastography as a cheaper clinical tool for assessing muscle stiffness in stroke rehabilitation.

title: The Effects of Power Dynamics in University-Community Partnerships
gloss: Studies power dynamics between undergraduate students and community members who co-lead sessions in a university-community partnership program, using surveys and focus groups to compare how each group views leadership, responsibility and power.

title: Identification of Optimal BAL Sample Processing Strategy Through Quantitative and Descriptive Comparative Assessment
gloss: Compares processing methods for bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) lung fluid samples to reduce human DNA and preserve microbial DNA, using qPCR, to find the best approach for sequencing the lung microbiome and supporting research on respiratory infections and lung diseases.

title: Biophysical Forces on VSMC Nucleus Regulate the Onset of Vascular Calcification Through Epigenetic Remodeling
gloss: Cell biology research on how mechanical forces acting on the nucleus of vascular smooth muscle cells change chromatin and epigenetics and push the cells toward a bone-like fate, driving vascular calcification (hardening of blood vessels), with the goal of finding new therapeutic targets.

title: Synthesis of Protein Aggregation Inhibitors for the Treatment of ALS
gloss: Medicinal chemistry project synthesizing new drug candidates for ALS (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) that inhibit toxic protein aggregation, modifying an existing compound scaffold to improve blood-brain barrier permeability and testing effects on motor neuron health in mouse models.

title: Food Cues and Brain-to-Gut Communication
gloss: A neuroscience study in mice of how food cues such as taste, sight and smell activate brain regions that prepare the gut for digestion, testing whether sensory cues alter glucose tolerance through brain-to-gut signaling.

title: Impact of Benefit-Framed Messages on Public Attitudes Towards Prison Education
gloss: A survey experiment testing whether messages highlighting the benefits of prison education, such as reduced recidivism and cost savings, change public support for prison education programs in the United States, relating public opinion to criminal justice reform and advocacy messaging.

title: Designing Metastable Protein Biosensors for Quality Control in Stress and Aging
gloss: Designs fluorescent protein biosensors from destabilized mutants of the enzyme DHFR to measure how the cell's protein quality control (proteostasis) network declines with aging and stress in C. elegans, relevant to neurodegenerative disease.

title: Portraitures of the people I adore (Photography)
gloss: A photography series of portraits of the artist's friends and family in Singapore and Qatar, showing them differently from how they are usually seen, with each photo paired with a description of how the photographer met the person.

title: Treatment of Epilepsy by the Inactivation of GABA-AT
gloss: Medicinal chemistry project synthesizing alkyl analogues of the epilepsy drug candidate CPP-115 to make GABA-AT inactivators more selective over ornithine aminotransferase, aiming to raise brain GABA levels and treat seizures through enzyme inhibition.

title: The Face That Drew a Thousand Swords (Digital Art)
gloss: A digital painting made in Procreate depicting Helen of Troy and Menelaus at the end of the Trojan War, using historically accurate Bronze Age dress and armor and placing Helen at the center to portray her as a complex mythic figure, both victim and instigator.

title: The Non-Typeable Haemophilus Influenzae Phasevarion Regulates Macrophage-Mediated Phagocytosis
gloss: Microbiology and immunology study of how the phasevarion, an epigenetic on/off gene-switching system in the bacterial pathogen non-typeable Haemophilus influenzae, affects how readily the bacteria are engulfed by human macrophages, an early step of the innate immune response to infection.

title: La Casa del Migrante (Documentary)
gloss: A short documentary about La Casa del Migrante, a home for Mexican immigrant artists in Chicago's Little Village that faces demolition by a developer. The film explores gentrification, urban displacement, eviction, and the value of community spaces.

title: Why Is She Speaking? (Poetry)
gloss: A protest poem about women speaking out against silencing, reclaiming suppressed female narratives and seeking agency in an exploitative media environment. Written as a tribute to Chinese women, it explores writing across languages, the loss of a mother tongue, and bearing witness.

title: Light as He Willed (Short Story)
gloss: A creative writing short story, performed as an excerpt, set during the 2021 protests in Cali, Colombia, following college students whose friend is taken by police. It explores youth hopelessness, police violence, family struggles, and connection to the Colombian landscape.

title: Femme, Queer, or Both: Asian American Narratives in the Midwest
gloss: A zine sharing interview-based stories of femme and queer Asian Americans living in the Midwest, inspired by zines from 1960s-70s Asian American student movements. It explores Asian American identity, community, and how diverse groups can build solidarity and connection.

title: Multipartite Entanglement in the Random Ising Chain
gloss: Theoretical condensed matter physics study of quantum entanglement between multiple subsystems in disordered (random) critical Ising spin chains, using numerical strong disorder renormalization group methods to compute entanglement negativity and mutual information and compare them with clean and other random quantum spin chains.

title: Toonana Mangwana, or, "We'll See Each Other Tomorrow" (Original Music)
gloss: An original music performance of two songwriting compositions exploring grief and loss during the COVID-19 pandemic, including a piece built around an archival recording of the composer's Zimbabwean grandmother singing a hymn, combining musicology, family memory and Shona heritage.

title: Against All Odds (Short Film)
gloss: A docufictional short film about the early life of Malala Yousafzai, portraying her activism for girls' education and her resistance to the Taliban in Pakistan's Swat Valley.

title: Melodies in Distance: Musicians in a Pandemic (Video Journalism)
gloss: A video journalism feature about how musicians in Qatar's Philharmonic Orchestra coped with isolation and creative block during the COVID-19 pandemic. Shot on an iPhone, it tells an untold story of the orchestra's struggles and recovery to show how professional artists keep creating through crisis.

title: Family of Approximations for Dirichlet L-functions
gloss: Number theory research developing a family of approximations to Dirichlet L-functions built from truncated Euler products, with numerical tests of accuracy and a proof of exponentially decaying error, aimed at studying L-function behavior in the critical strip of the complex plane.

title: Outsiders in the Promised Land: Young Adult Mizrahi Identity in Israel
gloss: Interview study of how young adult, college-educated Mizrahi Jews in Israel perceive their place in society and relate to their ethnic identity, examining ethnic inequality and discrimination between Mizrahi and Ashkenazi Jews, assimilation into dominant culture, and stereotypes.

title: The Great Outdoors? Discrimination Theory and Black Park Use
gloss: An anthropology project using historical anthropology and political ecology to examine why Black Americans use parks less, arguing that discrimination is the primary cause of low Black park use. It combines a literature review of leisure studies theories with case studies of Black national and state park use.

title: How Market Maker Inventory Affects Options Liquidity
gloss: A finance study of how options market makers' inventory risk affects market liquidity, using regressions on years of Chicago Board Options Exchange trading data and risk measures derived from the Black-Scholes model.

title: Wheying Your Options: Commercialization and Consumer Understandings of High-Protein Products
gloss: A study of how high-protein food products are marketed and how consumers understand protein claims on packaging, using semiotic analysis of products and interviews with college students about diet, nutrition beliefs and food marketing.

title: Machine Learning and Genome Editing to Resolve Variants of Uncertain Significance in
gloss: Develops a machine learning model and a functional lab assay to classify genetic variants of uncertain significance in TSC2, the gene behind tuberous sclerosis, a disorder causing drug-resistant epilepsy, to improve genetic diagnosis and access to precision mTOR-targeted therapies.

title: Role of DEPP1 in Regulating Lung Microvascular Endothelial Cell Autophagy Under Hypoxia
gloss: A cell biology study of how the gene DEPP1 controls autophagy in human lung blood vessel lining (endothelial) cells under low oxygen, using gene silencing in cultured cells, with relevance to pulmonary hypertension and other diseases of endothelial dysfunction.

title: Evaluating Crowdworkers' Ability to Identify Visual Triggers for Photosensitive Epilepsy in Media
gloss: A study of whether crowdworkers can identify flashes, fast transitions, patterns and other visual triggers for photosensitive epilepsy in online media. A survey had people judge GIFs, comparing their accuracy with machine detection algorithms to support web accessibility tools.

title: Understanding Intergenerational Trauma from Vietnamese Refugees through Graphic Memoirs
gloss: A literary analysis of how Asian American graphic memoirs, such as Thi Bui's The Best We Could Do and GB Tran's Vietnamerica, depict intergenerational trauma passed from Vietnamese refugee parents to their children, examining themes of repressed silence and internalized violence.

title: Touch Me and You'll Burn: Fire and Foresight in Statius' Achilleid
gloss: A literary analysis of fire and flame metaphors in Statius' Latin epic the Achilleid, comparing it with Ovid's Heroides to examine Achilles' passion for war and love and how female characters in classical epic foresee the hero's tragic fate but cannot prevent it.

title: The Impact of School Security on Student Wellbeing
gloss: A mixed-methods education study of how visible high school security measures such as metal detectors, cameras and security officers affect school climate and student wellbeing, using surveys and interviews with college students about their high school experiences.

title: Converting Carbon Dioxide into a Universal Chemical Building Block using Cell-Free Biomanufacturing
gloss: Uses cell-free biomanufacturing to build an enzyme pathway that converts carbon dioxide-derived formate into acetyl-CoA, a building block for industrial chemicals, as a carbon-negative climate solution. Enzymes are improved through protein engineering by mutagenesis and screened with mass spectrometry.

title: Quantification of opsin+ Neurons Reveals the Dynamics of Head Regeneration in
gloss: Developmental biology research on whole-body regeneration in the acoel worm Hofstenia miamia, using in situ hybridization of photoreceptor neurons to measure how brain size scales with body size during head regeneration, and applying this as a tool to test genes needed for regeneration via RNA interference.

title: Pervasive Citizenships: Cultural Citizenship, Transnationalism and Migrant Illegality in Angie Cruz's Dominicana
gloss: A literary analysis of Angie Cruz's novel Dominicana examining how cultural citizenship, transnationalism, and migrant illegality interact at the same time in the life of a Dominican immigrant in New York City, contributing to Latinx immigration and citizenship studies.

title: Social Networks in South Asian Healthy Lifestyle Intervention
gloss: A qualitative interview study of how family and peer social networks influenced heart-healthy lifestyle behavior change among South Asian American adults in a culturally adapted group lifestyle intervention, including social support, resistance from network members, and differences by gender and English proficiency.

title: A Pipeline Flows Both Ways: Contradictions of an Activist Trajectory
gloss: An autoethnographic honors thesis reflecting on the author's own path as an environmental and leftist activist, from high school sustainability work to Indigenous-led Line 3 pipeline resistance camps, exploring the contradictions of activism and social change for organizers and changemakers.

title: Examining the Utility of Refutation Replies to False Social Media Content
gloss: A psychology study of misinformation on social media, testing whether reply posts that refute false Tweets, including complete, partial, and socially aggressive corrections, reduce people's reliance on false information and help them recall correct facts.

title: Love Letter to a Trick
gloss: A queer studies and performance studies project on how Queer BIPOC kink practitioners and sex workers understand love, care and intimacy, using interviews, performance analysis and a literature review to challenge cisheteronormative ideas of romantic relationships and stigma around sex work and kink.

title: "Si No Te Gusta, Adiós": Mexican Temporal Assimilation in the Workplace
gloss: Interview-based sociology study of how first- and second-generation Mexican immigrants experience workplace barriers, assimilation and job mobility in factories in Decatur, Illinois, including Spanish-speaking hiring networks, undocumented work and bilingual promotion.

title: Race, Place, and Disaster: Newspaper Narration of Displaced Populations After Hurricane Katrina and the California Camp Fire
gloss: A sociology and media studies project analyzing how local and national newspapers portrayed people displaced by natural disasters, comparing Hurricane Katrina and the California Camp Fire, and how race, place, and disaster type shape stereotyping in news coverage.

title: The Role of Motive Disposition, Sense of Calling, and Parental Opinion in College Students' Career Decision-Making
gloss: A psychology survey study of how motivation, sense of calling, and parental influence shape college students' career decision-making, comparing students headed into business, healthcare, and education and exploring differences by race.

title: Affection, Friendship Quality, and Loneliness: A Dyadic Interaction Study
gloss: A psychology study of how adolescent and young adult friends experience feelings of affection during conflict and positive conversations, and how those feelings relate to friendship quality and loneliness, using recorded online conversations between pairs of friends and questionnaires.

title: Project MED (Medicine, Exposure, and Development): Promoting Access to Healthcare Education for Historically Underrepresented Groups Through Community Engagement, Sustainability, and Technology
gloss: An undergraduate-led pipeline program that introduces high school students from historically underrepresented groups to healthcare careers through workshops, mentoring and an opportunities database, with survey evaluation of student interest and outcomes. The aim is to diversify the healthcare workforce and reduce educational disparities.

title: Reducing Biofilm Formation through CRISPRi Mediated Mutation of Pseudomonas Aeruginosa for Use in Novel Theraputics
gloss: Microbiology and antibiotic resistance research using CRISPR interference to silence biofilm-forming genes in the opportunistic pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa, measuring effects on biofilm growth with crystal violet assays and optical coherence tomography imaging, toward new therapeutics for drug-resistant infections.

title: Psychotropic Medications in Foster Care: Documenting Trends in Drug Use, Patient Characteristics and Outcomes Using Large Administrative Data
gloss: Studies psychotropic medication use, including overprescribing and polypharmacy, among children in foster care, reviewing prior research and state and federal oversight policies and analyzing national Medicaid claims data on prescribing trends, patient characteristics and outcomes.

title: Modeling Individual Sleep Needs from Wearable-Device Data
gloss: Builds a mathematical two-process model of the sleep-wake cycle, combining sleep homeostasis and circadian rhythm, tuned with wearable actigraphy data and machine learning to predict how individuals are affected by and recover from sleep disruptions.

title: Exploring Climate Change Discourse on Social Media with Natural Language Processing
gloss: Uses natural language processing, including topic modeling and sentiment analysis with BERT, to compare how people discuss climate change on Twitter and Reddit, identifying the main subjects of conversation on each platform and tracking optimism or pessimism about climate over time.

title: The Effect of Work from Home on City Structures and Inequality
gloss: An urban economics study of how remote work since COVID-19 affects where people live and what they earn, using a difference-in-differences analysis to examine income gains, movement to the suburbs, and implications for income inequality and gentrification.

title: Moral Discourses, Regulated Bodies: Sex, the State, and Subjectivity in Cuba
gloss: Research assistance on a faculty book about how the Cuban state polices race, sex and gender, using testimonios from Afro-Cuban women about police harassment, criminalization as prostitutes, and incarceration, challenging the government's claim that socialism eradicated racism.

title: The Impact of Telehealth on Health Equity in Opioid Use Disorder Treatment
gloss: Health policy research on whether telehealth expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic improved or worsened access to opioid use disorder treatment for low-income Medicaid patients versus privately insured patients, using patient records to compare visits and buprenorphine prescribing and the role of broadband access.

title: Understanding and Improving Memory Outcomes in Children with Epilepsy
gloss: Develops fMRI memory tasks to map which side of the brain supports memory in children with temporal lobe epilepsy before epilepsy surgery, aiming to protect memory after surgery and replace the invasive Wada test. Involves pediatric neuroimaging and brain lateralization research.

title: Gender Equity Assessment with Gender IDEAL
gloss: Develops the second version of an organizational gender equity assessment that lets workplaces evaluate support for women and LGBTQ+ employees and receive evidence-based recommendations, including new questions on reproductive health services after the 2022 U.S. abortion ruling.

title: PyFlowBAT: An Open-Source Software Package for Performing High-Throughput Batch Analysis of Flow Cytometry Data
gloss: An open-source Python software package for fast, high-throughput batch analysis of flow cytometry data in synthetic biology, covering data processing, analysis and visualization, with templates for researchers with limited coding experience and validation on fluorescent protein expression data in mammalian cells.

title: Effects of Early Life Factors on the Infant Gut Microbiome
gloss: Studies how early life factors such as antibiotic use, breastfeeding, and birth mode shape the developing gut microbiome of infants, using fecal samples and survey data from infants in the Philippines to examine microbial diversity and its health implications.

title: Big and Small Nature: An Ethnographic Case Study of Lawns in Evanston, Illinois
gloss: An anthropology ethnography of how Evanston, Illinois residents relate to their suburban lawns, drawing on interviews, fieldwork and archival history of American lawn culture and suburbanization to examine how class, politics and sustainability shape native planting and human relationships with nature.

title: Nostalgia and the Arab Diaspora: Rewriting the Past into the Present, for the Future
gloss: Ethnographic study of Arab dance and music performance in the Chicago area, using interviews and fieldwork to examine how nostalgia builds community and identity between Arab immigrants and second- and third-generation Arab Americans in the diaspora.

title: The Anti-Critical Race Theory Movement
gloss: A political science study of the anti-critical race theory movement in US K-12 education, examining how local school boards and state legislation regulate discussion of race and racism and target transgender and gender nonconforming students, analyzed through the lens of biopolitics and biopower.

title: Determining Avenues to Improve Safety for College Students with Food Allergy
gloss: A nationwide online survey of college students with and without food allergies examining allergic reactions on campus, confidence using epinephrine auto-injectors, and interest in training and awareness efforts, to identify ways universities can improve food allergy education and safety.

title: White Students' (Dis)Engagement in Racial Identity and Allyship since Summer 2020
gloss: An interview study of white college students who identified as allies, examining how their engagement in racial justice work and support for Black Lives Matter changed after the 2020 George Floyd protests, and how they understand their white racial identity and allyship.

title: An Overview of Contemporary Social Influence of Hip Hop, Rap, and R&B
gloss: Research on the cultural and social influence of Hip Hop, rap, and R&B, including music, fashion, and visual art, and on rap pedagogy. The student interviewed contemporary Hip Hop and R&B artists about their teaching styles, inspirations, and audiences to support an educational resource for youth.

title: Your Ears Make Sounds! : Detecting Inner Ear Function Using the Sounds It Generates
