gloss: A psychology study of addiction recovery stories in Alcoholics Anonymous, using narrative identity theory to analyze how personal stories in the A.A. Big Book reflect the American redemptive self narrative and how storytelling and identity in recovery changed across its editions.

title: Tracking Through Time: A Computational Approach for Long-Term Neuron Tracking in Two-Photon Imaging
gloss: A computational pipeline for tracking the same individual neurons across multiple days of two-photon calcium imaging in the mouse prefrontal cortex, enabling long-term analysis of how neural activity patterns change over time, such as as mice acclimate to an experimental environment.

title: Isotopic tracers of ocean acidification and extinction in Cretaceous foraminifera
gloss: Geochemistry and paleoclimate research using calcium isotope measurements of fossil plankton shells from a South Atlantic deep-sea drilling core to test whether ocean acidification caused a mass extinction of marine calcifying organisms during an Early Cretaceous warming event, as an analog for modern climate change.

title: Exploring Aberrant Vimentin Expression and Localization in Glioblastoma
gloss: Cancer biology research on glioblastoma, an aggressive brain tumor, examining how chemotherapy (temozolomide) treatment changes the expression and cellular location of vimentin, a cytoskeletal protein linked to tumor cell migration and invasion, using patient-derived tumor cell lines.

title: How Large Language Models Can Help Us Study Spatial Language
gloss: Uses large language models to automatically code children's and parents' spatial language, a factor in STEM learning, and compares this approach with human coding and bag-of-words software (LIWC) on datasets such as parent-child reflections from the Chicago Children's Museum.

title: Patterns of inflammation are associated with patterns of fecal-derived metabolites across human and nonhuman primate gut microbiomes
gloss: Compares how gut microbiomes of humans and nonhuman primates (baboons, howler monkeys, capuchins) affect human immune responses, exposing cultured human blood to fecal extracts and measuring inflammatory cytokines. Explores links between gut microbes, their metabolites, and immune regulation across primate evolution.

title: Electric Utility Companies and Green Bonds; Energy Transition and the Greenium
gloss: An economics study of whether electric utility companies pay lower borrowing costs (a green premium, or greenium) when they issue green bonds instead of conventional bonds. It compares matched bond yields to assess sustainable finance and debt financing for the energy transition.

title: Structural Inequities in COVID-19 Hospitalization: Evidence from the All of Us Research Program
gloss: Uses national All of Us Research Program data to examine how race, ethnicity, age, income, education and neighborhood deprivation relate to COVID-19 hospitalization risk, highlighting structural and social inequities in U.S. health outcomes.

title: Childhood Household Wealth Mobility and Mental Health in Young Adulthood: Evidence from the Cebu Longitudinal Health and Nutrition Survey
gloss: Studies how changes in household wealth during childhood relate to depression and perceived stress in young adulthood, using birth cohort data from the Cebu Longitudinal Health and Nutrition Survey in the Philippines to link childhood socioeconomic mobility with adult mental health.

title: Coal, Culture, and Neostalgia: Reframing Industrial Heritage Identities for a Just Transition
gloss: A rhetorical analysis of how Kentucky folk musicians use music and storytelling to challenge coal industry narratives and reshape Appalachian identity, examining a short film by The Local Honeys and its role in promoting a just energy transition away from coal.

title: California's Connection Conundrum: DLR Technology Utility
gloss: An energy policy analysis arguing that California should expand mandates and incentives for dynamic line rating technology on power transmission lines, to increase grid capacity for connecting renewable energy and to help detect conditions that could spark wildfires.

title: The Impact of Guided Relaxation on Sleep Quality and Mood in College Students with Sleep Disturbances
gloss: A psychology study testing whether listening to a brief guided mindfulness relaxation audio before bed helps college students with sleep problems fall asleep faster and feel better the next day, using at-home sleep tracking headbands and daily mood surveys.

title: Narratives of Resistance: Centering Student Voices in a Time of Crisis
gloss: Qualitative analysis of narrative reflections from first-year Black college students on living through the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2020 George Floyd protests, using Critical Race Theory to examine racial identity, activism, trauma, resistance, and community in higher education.

title: Wastewater Bacterium Comamonas testosteroni: A Promising Platform for Microbial Plastic Recycling
gloss: Tests whether a wastewater bacterium, Comamonas testosteroni, can biodegrade low-density polyethylene (LDPE) plastic as an alternative to mechanical recycling, and how adding acetate as a co-substrate affects bacterial growth and plastic degradation.

title: Darren v. Blaine: the effects of listener stereotypes on the perception of sibilant duration
gloss: A sociolinguistics experiment on whether listeners' stereotypes about a speaker's sexual orientation change how they perceive sibilant (s-sound) duration in gay men's speech, using speech perception tasks with audio and visual stimuli of a real speaker.

title: TEAMs Human-AI Interaction Project
gloss: Studies how adding an AI teammate changes communication patterns in small human teams working on problem-solving and creativity tasks, using a Wizard-of-Oz agent and relational hyperevent network models of who speaks to whom in team conversations.

title: Cracking the Code: Enhancing Detection of Reading Disorders
gloss: Research on improving the identification and classification of specific learning disorders in children's word reading and reading comprehension, including developing a parent questionnaire in REDCap on family history, home environment and language background, and visualizing descriptive data about the questionnaire items.

title: Engineering Extracellular Vesicles to Optimize Biotherapeutic Delivery
gloss: Bioengineering research on extracellular vesicles as drug delivery vehicles, testing whether coating vesicles with mucin biopolymers and adding T cell targeting molecules reduces unwanted uptake by nontarget cells and improves targeted delivery of biotherapeutics.

title: Environmental Changes After European Settlement Inferred from Sediment Chemistry of a Wisconsin Lake
gloss: Paleolimnology study using lake sediment cores from a Wisconsin lake to reconstruct environmental history since European settlement, tracing how deforestation, agriculture and fertilizer use caused nutrient loading, eutrophication and algal blooms through sediment geochemistry and stable isotopes.

title: Exploring Low-Density and High-Density Water Populations Using Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) Spectroscopy
gloss: Uses NMR spectroscopy to experimentally detect low-density and high-density populations of liquid water, measuring oxygen-17 chemical shifts and relaxation rates across temperatures from -15C to 25C. The work studies the structure of liquid water as a foundation for later research on water-protein interactions.

title: Mother-Child book-sharing activity differs across Taiwanese and American Cultures
gloss: A cross-cultural study comparing how Taiwanese Mandarin-speaking and American English-speaking mothers and their preschool children tell stories during shared book reading, examining how culture shapes parent language scaffolding and child narrative development, with implications for pediatric language assessment and parent coaching.

title: Rareh Gyals: Outcasts or Pioneers? A Close Analysis of Time-Defiant Krio Speech Trends and Its Implications for the Future
gloss: A sociolinguistic study of how sex workers in Sierra Leone use and reshape the Krio language to express exclusion, defiance and identity, drawing on oral histories, ethnography and documentary analysis of language, gender and power.

title: Cramps and Choices: How Young Adolescents Navigate Medication Usage and Absences Due to Menstrual Pain in the Two Years After Menarche
gloss: A study of how young adolescent girls cope with menstrual pain in the two years after their first period, following a cohort to see when they take pain medication or miss physical activities, social activities and school, and what factors shape those choices.

title: Assent and Negation Language and Emotional Experiences in Marriages and Friendships
gloss: A psychology study of how agreeing and negating words in conversation relate to emotions in close relationships, comparing married couples and friends during conflict and pleasant discussions using linguistic word-count analysis of videotaped lab conversations.

title: Upcycling rubber waste through dynamic bond incorporation
gloss: A chemistry and materials science project on recycling waste tire rubber by adding dynamic covalent crosslinks, turning ground-up rubber into a reprocessable, self-healing polymer network that can be pressed into new films, as a sustainable alternative to landfilling rubber and reducing plastic and polymer pollution.

title: The Experiences of Dyslexic Students in Higher Education
gloss: A qualitative study using surveys and interviews of dyslexic college students across U.S. higher education institutions, examining their access to academic accommodations, how well disability support services meet their needs, and the social and emotional effects of dyslexia, including stigma and anxiety.

title: Rethinking Moral Disagreements: A Model for Mapping the Divergence of Belief
gloss: A philosophy project in metaethics that builds a model for mapping why people and philosophers disagree about morality, tracing disagreements to hidden assumptions about what moral judgments target and aim to achieve, and applying it to ethical theories such as utilitarianism, Kantian deontology, subjectivism and divine command theory.

title: Go With the Flow: Evaluation of Welfare Gains to Proportional Surface Water Rights
gloss: An economics study of surface water markets that uses a bargaining model and simulations to compare the welfare effects of proportional versus fixed-quantity water rights, considering trading costs, variable water supply, urban growth and climate resilience.

title: Measuring the Impact of High School COVID-19 Policies On Enrollment Changes
gloss: An economics study of how COVID-19 school reopening policies, including virtual, hybrid and in-person instruction, affected student enrollment at public and private high schools in Cook County and Chicago, and what this reveals about parents' schooling choices during the pandemic.

title: Not Just Sweet Treats: Exploring the Treatment of People with Celiac Disease Through the Lens of French and Italian Gluten-Free Bakery and Restaurant Owners
gloss: An interview-based qualitative study of owners and employees at dedicated gluten-free bakeries and restaurants in Paris and Rome, exploring how food workers interact with people with celiac disease and the community, emotional connection, and changing perceptions of celiac that emerge in these spaces.

title: Manoomin/Psii and Water Relations in the Otter Tail Watershed: A Community-Driven Hydrologic Study
gloss: A community-partnered hydrology study of how groundwater and surface water fluctuations affect wild rice (Manoomin/Psii), a plant sacred to Anishinaabe and Dakota communities, at lakes in Minnesota's Otter Tail watershed, using stream gauges and piezometers with White Earth Ojibwe partners.

title: A Different World: How Black Men Perceive their Belonging at Northwestern
gloss: An interview-based qualitative study of how Black undergraduate men at Northwestern, a predominantly white institution, experience academic and social belonging, including shifting friendships, feeling underprepared in STEM, Queer Black students' isolation, and worries about the future of DEI programs that support them.

title: Detangling Entanglements: Using topology to mechanically tame polymers
gloss: Materials science study of how polymer chain entanglements (network topology) control the mechanical strength, toughness, and stretchability of soft polymer networks, tuning entanglements with solvent to make tougher soft materials for uses like soft robotics, tissue engineering, and 3D printing.

title: Emergency Medical Services and Behavioral Health: Evaluating National Protocols for Psychiatric Care
gloss: A review of how national EMS protocols, textbooks and training curricula prepare EMTs and paramedics to handle psychiatric and behavioral health emergencies, finding training gaps and proposing reforms to improve prehospital mental health crisis care.

title: Tuning Structural Color in Ethyl Cellulose - Poly(Acrylic Acid) via Molecular Weight Blending
gloss: Materials science research on sustainable, pigment-free structural color from self-assembled ethyl cellulose, studying how blending different polymer molecular weights changes the color of cast films, as a non-toxic alternative to synthetic textile dyes.

title: Characterization of Phosphonate-Based Metal-Organic Frameworks for Atmospheric Water Harvesting
gloss: Uses solid-state NMR spectroscopy to study how nickel phosphonate metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) adsorb water, assessing these porous materials for atmospheric water harvesting to provide clean water.

title: Shaping the Gut: The Role of Socioeconomic and Household Environments in Microbiome Development Throughout Early Life
gloss: Studies how household socioeconomic status and environment, including intergenerational wealth, shape gut microbiome development in children in the Philippines (Cebu, Southeast Asia), using longitudinal health survey data to link family wealth and microbial exposure to early-life gut bacterial diversity and composition.

title: A Kantian Perspective on Plea Bargaining in the United States
gloss: A philosophy and criminal justice ethics project applying Immanuel Kant's theory of punishment to plea bargaining in U.S. courts, drawing on interviews with attorneys to argue for reforms prioritizing proportionate punishment, legal legitimacy, and resisting efficiency-driven justice.

title: Parenting with ADHD Symptoms: Investigating Warmth, Discipline, and Their Impact on Children with ADHD
gloss: A psychology survey study of how mothers' own ADHD symptoms relate to their parenting, including warmth and positive and negative discipline, and to behavior problems in their young children, with a look at gender differences in child ADHD diagnosis and symptom severity.

title: Photons to Fuel: Harnessing Light to Produce Hydrogen by Designing SiO2/TiO2 Photocatalysts
gloss: Chemistry and materials research designing silica-coated titanium dioxide photocatalysts that use light to release hydrogen from liquid organic hydrogen carriers, comparing coating methods and how catalyst surface structure affects hydrogen production for sustainable clean energy and fuel storage.

title: Injectable Synthetic Bone Marrow Grafts (ISBM)
gloss: Develops an injectable synthetic hydrogel bone marrow graft that temporarily supports white blood cell production for patients awaiting bone marrow transplants. Compares hydrogel chemistries for stem cell engraftment and survival and tests the graft in a mouse model.

title: Leo Tolstoy on Law, Morality, and Religion
gloss: A study of Leo Tolstoy's Christian religious-philosophical critique of Russian and Western legal systems, examining his view of courts and law as tools of oppression contrary to love and non-violence, and his call to dissolve state institutions, with relevance to modern debates on justice and mass incarceration.

title: Say what again?: Investigating the intelligibility of Formula 1 driver speech between situations, contexts, and language backgrounds
gloss: A linguistics project building a corpus of Formula 1 driver radio communications to study speech intelligibility under high-stress conditions, comparing in-car radio, post-race interviews and studio interviews, and how listeners' first- or second-language English affects comprehension.

title: This Wasn't on the Syllabus: The Hidden Curriculum of Office Hours
gloss: A survey study of how Northwestern undergraduates use faculty office hours, examining whether race, gender, and reasons for attending relate to students' academic self-concept and sense of belonging, and framing office hours as a hidden curriculum of informal networking and student-faculty relationships.

title: Shortwave Radio: Sublime Communication and Community of the Cold War
gloss: A history of shortwave radio listening in North America from the 1960s to today, examining how Cold War international broadcasts and propaganda shaped listeners' sense of politics, security and global community, drawing on hobbyist publications, online forums and interviews with shortwave listeners.

title: Spatial-Temporal Profiling of Scn2a in the Mammalian Cerebellum
gloss: Maps where and when the epilepsy- and autism-linked sodium channel gene SCN2A is expressed in the developing human cerebellum, using spatial RNA profiling of prenatal and adolescent brain tissue to identify which cerebellar cell types express it during brain development.

title: Self-Perceptions of Socioeconomic Status at NU
gloss: An interview study of how Northwestern undergraduates' perceptions of their own socioeconomic status and class identity change after enrolling at an elite, wealthy university, and how social class shapes friendships, belonging and college adjustment.

title: Emotional intensity affects the interpretation of verbal frequency expressions
gloss: A psycholinguistics experiment on how people interpret vague frequency words like "often" and "rarely" as numerical percentages, testing whether the emotional intensity of a scenario shifts those estimates. Relevant to language comprehension, emotion, and survey design.

title: Exploring the Contributions of Contextual Factors to Students' Performance on Statewide Achievement Tests
gloss: Examines how neighborhood characteristics relate to Illinois public school students' performance on statewide achievement tests in grades 3 to 8, linking school data from the Illinois State Board of Education with U.S. Census data and the Child Opportunity Index to describe neighborhood conditions.

title: From Persecution to Prosperity: Iraqi Chaldeans, Forced Migration, and Search for Home
gloss: A history of the Iraqi Chaldean community's forced migration from religious persecution in Iraq to Metro Detroit, drawing on interviews and archival sources to examine diaspora community building, assimilation, and preservation of Christian faith, language, and identity in the United States.

title: Willingness to Pay for Eco-Labeled Products: A Study of Green Seal Certification and Consumer Trust
gloss: A survey experiment on whether U.S. consumers will pay more for eco-labeled, Green Seal certified household products, examining how environmental knowledge, trust in eco-labels, and demographics shape green purchasing behavior and the gap between environmental attitudes and buying choices.

title: RNA Metabolic Labeling in Lysed Yeast Cells.
gloss: Develops a method to measure gene transcription in lysed yeast cells by labeling newly made RNA with 4-thiouracil and detecting it with a fluorescent dye instead of radioactive nucleotides. The goal is a way to study essential transcription proteins by inhibiting them without killing the cells.

title: Synthesizing PEDOT:PSS Adsorbed on hBN Nanoplatelets for Flexible Electronics Applications
gloss: Develops a method to coat 2D materials like hexagonal boron nitride with the conductive polymer PEDOT:PSS, creating mixed ionic-electronic conductors for flexible electronics and energy storage devices such as batteries.

title: Challenging the Tourist: How the Experiences of Growing Up in Hawai'i Influence Engagement with Dominant Narratives about Home while in the Continental United States
gloss: Qualitative study using interviews and focus groups with college students from Hawai'i attending school in the continental U.S., examining how growing up in Hawai'i shapes their views of race, indigeneity, and colonialism and how they respond to tourist narratives and misconceptions about their home.

title: Experiences of Younger Sisters of Eating Disorder Patients
gloss: A qualitative interview study of how younger sisters are affected when an older sister has an eating disorder, examining family dynamics, sibling relationships, and the siblings' own identity, mental health, and relationship with food and body image.

title: Translating Culture: Ginseng and the Global Circulation of Knowledge between Qing China and Enlightenment Europe
gloss: A history of science project on how Chinese medical knowledge about ginseng was translated and reshaped in early 18th-century European scientific writing, comparing Qing Chinese herbal texts with a Jesuit botanical report to examine cross-cultural knowledge exchange between China and Enlightenment Europe.

title: Does Naming Support 12-Month-Old Infants' Individuation of Own- and Other-Race Faces?
gloss: A developmental psychology study of whether giving distinct names to faces helps 12-month-old infants tell individual people apart, comparing own-race and other-race faces to examine how language interacts with the other-race effect in infant face processing.

title: Spatial Dynamics of Macrophage Responses to Salmonella Typhimurium
gloss: Studies how spatial proximity and local density of neighboring macrophages influence inflammatory gene expression and signaling during Salmonella infection, using Python analysis of single-cell imaging data that preserves spatial information. Explores cell-to-cell communication among immune cells in bacterial infection.

title: Characterization of Optical Modulators for Neural Implant and Satellite Technologies
gloss: Electrical and optical characterization of semiconductor quantum well optical modulators, measuring current-voltage and capacitance-voltage behavior under laser illumination, for compact low-power devices used in neural implants detecting brain signals and in satellite communication.

title: Clinically-Validated Automatic Lumbar T1-Weighted Spinal MRI Segmentation Tool via an Attention U-Net Algorithm
gloss: Develops a deep learning tool that automatically segments lumbar spine MRI scans (sagittal T1-weighted images) using an attention U-Net, comparing it against other neural network architectures and loss functions and validating its accuracy with ratings from neuroradiologists.

title: Sounding Out Stress: The Impact of Music and Breathwork on Teen Well-being
gloss: Pilot study of a group singing and breathwork program as a music intervention to reduce stress and anxiety and improve well-being in high school students, measured with wearable heart rate sensors, mood tracking, anxiety surveys and interviews.

title: Respiratory Deficits Uncovered During the Six-Minute Walk Test in Children with Congenital Central Hypoventilation Syndrome
gloss: Clinical study of how children with congenital central hypoventilation syndrome, a rare genetic breathing disorder, respond to exercise, comparing blood oxygen and carbon dioxide levels during and after a six-minute walk test with healthy children to assess exertion-related respiratory deficits.

title: Canceling the Continued Influence Effect: The Role of Source Valence Perceptions in Retraction Acceptance
gloss: A psychology experiment on misinformation and the continued influence effect, testing whether liking or disliking a news source affects whether people keep believing a cause after it has been retracted or corrected, and whether offering an alternative explanation helps.

title: Evidence, Expertise, and Exploration: Politics of Knowledge in Gender Therapy
gloss: A sociological case study of competing approaches to therapy for transgender people, comparing gender affirmative, gender exploratory, and gender identity change therapy models in how they frame trans identity, use scientific evidence, and shape power and knowledge about gender diversity.

title: Pathways to Parenthood: Examining the Role of Insurance for Same-Sex Female Couples Accessing Assisted Reproductive Technologies
gloss: A mixed-methods study using surveys and interviews to examine how health insurance creates barriers for lesbian and same-sex female couples seeking fertility treatment and assisted reproductive technologies, including discriminatory infertility definitions, high costs, and reliance on employer benefits, in the context of LGBTQ discrimination.

title: The Kids Are Alright: College Environments, Student Wellbeing, and the Role of Institutional Selectivity
gloss: A psychology survey study of college student anxiety and mental health, testing whether personal factors like fear of failure and achievement motivation or the campus environment and school selectivity better predict anxiety among Gen Z undergraduates at elite and less selective universities.

title: Combating Antibiotic Resistance Using Cobalt(III) Schiff Base Complexes as Metallo-vLactamase Inhibitors
gloss: Studies cobalt(III) Schiff base metal complexes as inhibitors of metallo-beta-lactamase enzymes such as NDM-1, which bacteria use to destroy penicillin-type antibiotics. A library of complexes was tested to find compounds that could be paired with antibiotics to overcome antibiotic resistance.

title: Mechanisms of GABAergic ipRGC in light sensitivity
gloss: Neuroscience research on how GABA-releasing light-sensitive retinal neurons (ipRGCs) dampen sensitivity to dim light in mice, examining circadian behavior and pupil responses in knockout mice and mapping activated brain regions with c-fos staining and confocal imaging.

title: Human Immune Response To Microbes Varies Based on Gut Microbiome Composition
gloss: Studies how gut microbiome composition relates to human immune and inflammatory responses, exposing human blood immune cells to fecal metabolites from humans and non-human primates and measuring cytokine levels alongside 16S rRNA sequencing of gut microbes.

title: Triapine (3AP) as a Radiosensitizing Agent in Breast Cancer Brain Metastasis
gloss: Cancer biology lab research testing whether the drug Triapine, an RRM2 ribonucleotide reductase inhibitor, makes breast cancer cells that spread to the brain more sensitive to whole-brain radiation therapy, by measuring DNA damage and cell survival in cultured brain-metastatic breast cancer cells.

title: Exploring the Impact of Ceramide Synthesis Enzymes on Atopic Dermatitis Severity: Alterations in Serine Palmitoyl Transferase Composition Underlie the Poor Epidermal Barrier in Atopic Dermatitis
gloss: Dermatology research on how changes in ceramide-making enzymes contribute to the weakened skin barrier in atopic dermatitis (eczema), using patient skin RNA data, cytokine-treated skin explants, and a knockout mouse model to test effects on eczema severity and itch.

title: Scenes of green: Neighborhood social cohesion and the measurement of greenspace exposure in Evanston, Illinois
gloss: Survey and geospatial study of how urban greenspace exposure relates to neighborhood social cohesion and mental health in Evanston, Illinois, comparing subjective survey measures, satellite-derived measures and Google Street View imagery of visible greenery to assess how measurement method affects results.

title: An Analysis of Digital Memes, Research Methods, and Cultural Impact
gloss: A literature review of communication studies research on internet memes since 2010, analyzing the research methods and frameworks used to study memes and summarizing how memes and social media humor affect cultural communities and events.

title: Observing Excessive Heat-Related Mortality in Chicago with High Resolution Temperature Models
gloss: Builds a high-resolution spatiotemporal temperature model of Chicago from community-collected Heat Watch data to estimate excessive heat-related mortality, and compares it with a model based on Daymet temperature data. The project examines the urban heat island effect and heat vulnerability for public health and equitable climate policy.

title: Exploring Correlates of Environmental Behavior Across Different Contexts
gloss: A social psychology study of how emotional attachment to a place relates to people's willingness to take climate action, and whether climate change messages framed around local versus global impacts change that link. Uses surveys and experiments with Northwestern students and a nationwide sample of U.S. adults.

title: The Perceptions and Experiences of Attraction in College Students
gloss: A qualitative interview study of how college students conceptualize and experience romantic and sexual attraction, comparing gay, lesbian and straight men and women and examining how sexual identity and social scripts shape the way people think about attraction and choose relationship partners.

title: The Impact of Informal Learning Experiences on Middle School Students' Communication About Climate Change: A Proposal
gloss: A proposed study of how an informal climate change education field trip affects how middle school students talk about climate science, comparing their word use across school years and between coastal, inland, urban and rural schools.

title: Resources for Promoting Resilience and Belongingness within High Schoolers
gloss: A survey study of high school students in Chicago Public Schools assessing whether school mental health resources are accessible and effective, and which resilience and protective factors, such as belonging and school counselors, marginalized students find most helpful for their mental health and suicide prevention.

title: Predicting Circumboreal Stonefly Responses to Climate Change Using Species Distribution Modeling and Population Genetics
gloss: Studies how Arctic and boreal stoneflies, aquatic insects at high extinction risk, will respond to climate change, combining DNA sequencing and population genetics with species distribution modeling of past, present and future habitat to guide insect conservation.

title: Microtubule Acetylation Modulates Endothelial Cell Response to Shear Stress
gloss: Cell biology study of how chemical modifications of microtubules, especially acetylation, help blood vessel endothelial cells sense and respond to blood flow shear stress, using flow experiments, drug inhibitors and CRISPR gene knockouts to examine cytoskeleton changes and cell alignment.

title: Music, Protest, and The People: Developments of Nueva Cancion Chilena From Violeta Parra to Allende's Election
gloss: A history thesis on Chile's Nueva Cancion folk music movement from the 1950s to 1970, tracing how protest music came to be seen as the authentic voice of the people and of leftist politics, from Violeta Parra's folk revival to Salvador Allende's election, using archival sources and the music itself.

title: Neurophysiological contributors to polarizing trends of speech-in-noise perception in Autism
gloss: Studies why some autistic people struggle to hear speech in background noise while others excel, testing whether differences in how the brain encodes sound, measured with EEG frequency following responses, explain this variability in speech-in-noise perception across autistic and non-autistic participants.

title: Leaf wax patterns reveal landscape changes through an extreme climate shift in southern Greenland
gloss: Paleoclimate research using leaf wax lipid biomarkers from southern Greenland lake sediments to reconstruct how vegetation, hydrology and landscapes changed during the Younger Dryas abrupt cooling event, as an analog for future Arctic climate change.

title: Developing an Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR) Based Assay to Study Structure-specific Positron Emission Tomography (PET) Ligand Binding to Tau Fibrils In Vitro
gloss: Develops an electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy assay to measure how a spin-labeled PET imaging ligand binds to tau protein fibrils from Alzheimer's disease versus other tauopathies, using a cyclodextrin to prevent ligand self-aggregation, aiming to improve PET imaging for Alzheimer's diagnosis.

title: A Complete Workflow for Determining the Axonal Projection Patterns of Neurons
gloss: Neuroscience methods project developing a workflow to trace and computationally reconstruct axon projections in whole mouse brains without slicing, using brain clearing, fluorescent labeling, tissue expansion, microscopy imaging and open-source reconstruction software, to study neuronal connectivity in areas such as the prefrontal cortex.

title: Electrochemical Fluorination of Organic Molecules via Phenothiazine
gloss: Develops a green electrochemical method for adding fluorine-containing trifluoromethyl groups to aromatic rings in drug-like molecules, using phenothiazine as a redox mediator instead of expensive metal catalysts. Relevant to organic synthesis, fluorination chemistry, and medicinal chemistry.

title: The Impact of Sports Participation on Gender Expression and Self-Perceptions of Female Athletes
gloss: A sociology study using qualitative interviews with Northwestern varsity female student-athletes to explore how playing women's sports shapes their identity, gender expression, and sense of femininity, and how they balance athlete and gender norms.

title: Where is the perro?: Developing an inclusive approach to analyze bilingual communication
gloss: Studies early language development in 2-year-old Spanish-English bilingual children by developing a behavioral coding scheme that tracks both spoken language and nonverbal gestures in caregiver-child interactions, aiming to improve screening and diagnosis of communication disorders in bilingual kids.

title: Light-enhanced propane dehydrogenation using plasmonic copper-platinum supported nanoparticles
gloss: Chemistry research on using light to drive catalytic conversion of propane into propylene with plasmonic copper nanoparticles doped with platinum on silica, aiming to make production of this plastic building block more sustainable than conventional steam cracking.

title: The Role of Cell Structure Proteins in Heart Health
gloss: Studies how the nuclear membrane protein SUN2, part of the LINC complex linking the nucleus and cytoskeleton, affects heart function, using electrocardiogram data from knockout mice to examine cardiac electrical conduction and arrhythmia risk.

title: 'Birdvibe': Examining Interdomain Representations of Birds in 19th and 20th Century Classical Music
gloss: A music theory and music cognition study of how 19th and 20th century classical composers portray birds through their size, movement and character rather than birdsong, analyzing melody, contour, ornamentation and instrumentation and comparing cognitive theories of how music conveys non-musical meaning.

title: Data Centers as Grid Assets: Microeconomics of Virtual Power Plants
gloss: An energy economics study of whether battery storage at data centers can provide reliable backup power while earning revenue in electricity markets, using an optimization model of the Texas ERCOT grid to weigh profit against reliability and treat data centers as virtual power plants.

title: Global Climate Governance: Finding the Meaning Behind Loss & Damage at COP29
gloss: An ethnographic study of international climate negotiations at the UN COP29 climate conference, examining how countries and affected communities define 'loss and damage' and how disagreement over its meaning shapes the UN fund meant to compensate communities harmed by climate change.

title: EEG and Video Monitoring via Open-Caged Monitoring to Understand Sickness Behavior in Mice During Sleep
gloss: A neuroscience study in mice comparing slow-wave EEG brain activity during inflammation-induced sickness behavior, a model for delirium, with normal NREM sleep, using combined EEG and video monitoring with automated pose estimation to analyze brain activity and behavior together.

title: Exploring Relationships Between Digital Work Arrangements and Well-Being: The Mediating Roles of Social Support, Work-Home Conflict, and Experienced Awe
gloss: An organizational psychology survey study of how remote, hybrid, and digital nomad work arrangements relate to worker well-being, testing social support, work-home conflict, and experiences of awe as mediators.

title: Combinatory Siglec-6 and Siglec-8 Treatments on IgE-Mediated Mast Cell Activation
gloss: Immunology lab study testing whether antibody treatments targeting the inhibitory receptors Siglec-6 and Siglec-8, alone and combined, can reduce allergic IgE-mediated mast cell activation, measured with flow cytometry, aimed at treating Type 2 inflammatory diseases.

title: He Hit Me But It Felt Like Love: An Analysis of the Cultural Messaging in Law and Order: Special Victims Unit's Depictions of Intimate Partner Violence
gloss: A media studies thesis analyzing how the TV series Law & Order: SVU depicts intimate partner violence and domestic abuse, examining the cultural messages these portrayals send about survivors, victim blaming, and abuser accountability, and framing IPV as a public health issue.

title: Unequal Shares: Airbnb and Racial Dynamics in Chicago Neighborhoods
gloss: A study of how Airbnb shapes racial inequality and economic opportunity in Chicago neighborhoods, using Airbnb listing data and census demographic data to compare pricing, reviews and revenue for minority hosts and in historically Black areas like Bronzeville.

title: Effect of water chemistry on the phosphorus adsorption by PEARL
gloss: Studies how water chemistry, including pH and dissolved salts, affects phosphorus removal by PEARL, an adsorbent made of cellulose sponge coated with iron nanoparticles. The work addresses nutrient pollution and eutrophication through low-cost water treatment and phosphorus recovery.

title: Metabolic Consequences of Huntington's Disease in Mice Brain and Skeletal Muscle
gloss: Studies how Huntington's disease alters glucose metabolism in the brain and skeletal muscle of a mouse model, using isotope-labeled glucose tracing with bulk and spatial metabolomics to examine energy pathways like glycolysis and the TCA cycle and treat the neurodegenerative disease as a whole-body condition.

title: Hitchhiking en Botella: Race, Gender, and Politics of Mobility in Cuba
gloss: Research assistant work on race, gender, and sex work in revolutionary Cuba, including translating Afro-Cuban women's testimonios (oral narratives) using oral history methods and an intersectional, Black feminist lens. The project is framed around the politics of mobility and hitchhiking in Cuba.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation with Wireless, Battery Free Pacemaker
gloss: Develops a medical device combining a catheter-delivered artificial aortic valve with a wireless, battery-free cardiac pacemaker mounted on the valve stent, so heart valve replacement and pacing happen in one minimally invasive procedure, tested in pig models.

title: Exploring Study and Participant Characteristics Across Studies Focused on the Executive Function Skills of Children with Specific Reading Comprehension Deficits
gloss: A meta-analysis of research on executive function skills, such as working memory, inhibition and planning, in children with specific reading comprehension deficits compared with typical readers. It describes study and participant characteristics, including age and language spoken, and compares linguistic and non-linguistic executive function measures.

title: Exploring the therapeutic potential of single-chain variable fragment antibodies in inhibiting amyloid plaque growth in Alzheimer's disease
gloss: Tests an antibody-based gene therapy for Alzheimer's disease, using virus-delivered antibody fragments to slow amyloid plaque growth in mouse models and examining effects on neuron damage, tau pathology and brain immune cells.

title: Examining discoidin domain receptor as a regulator of planarian eye regeneration
gloss: Studies how stem cells rebuild eyes during regeneration in planarian flatworms, using single-cell RNA sequencing to identify the gene discoidin domain receptor (ddr) as a regulator of eye cell differentiation and eye placement, with relevance to stem cell therapies.

title: Beyond the Black Box: The Use of Formal Channels in Addressing Surveillance Harm, as Shown Through the Chicago Police Department's CLEAR "Gang Database."
gloss: A qualitative study of how courts, ordinances and other formal legal channels fail to address police surveillance harms, using litigation over the Chicago Police Department's gang database as a case study, and how activists use lawsuits to build public knowledge and advocacy.

title: Development of High Porosity Silica Aerogels
gloss: Develops new lab methods for making ultra-low-density, highly uniform silica aerogels, a porous materials science project. The aerogels are meant for low-temperature physics experiments using liquid helium-3 to study how impurities affect superconductivity and unconventional superconductors.

title: Abolitionist Futures vs. The Status Quo: Northwestern racial/ethnic affinity spaces and Black and Brown students' post-undergrad goals
gloss: A sociology study of how campus racial and ethnic affinity spaces shape Black and Brown Northwestern students' goals for their communities and lives after college, using surveys and interviews to contrast abolitionist, liberation-oriented aims with aims of ascent within existing systems.

title: Conformational Dynamics of Enzyme Topoisomerase I in its Interactions with DNA
gloss: Biophysics study of how the DNA-relaxing enzyme topoisomerase I changes shape as it binds and acts on DNA, using single-molecule FRET fluorescence to track movements between its domains, with the aim of informing better cancer drug inhibitors.

title: CoGli-GOPEI Reduces Cancer Cell Migration Activated by Cutaneous Mechanosensory Nerves
gloss: Develops and tests a nanoparticle-delivered cobalt-DNA drug that targets the Hedgehog signaling pathway as a noninvasive alternative to surgery for basal cell carcinoma skin cancer, measuring how well it reduces cancer cell migration compared with existing inhibitors.

title: "To be A Loudmouth American Woman": South Asian American Mothers, Cultural Resistance, and Theatrical Disruption
gloss: A theater and performance studies paper on how South Asian American immigrant mothers are portrayed in plays and stand-up comedy, examining how these performances challenge stereotypes of silent, subservient desi motherhood and resist cultural assimilation and patriarchy through feminist and postcolonial perspectives.

title: Mindfulness Coaching: Do the coaches experience benefits themselves?
gloss: A psychology study of whether peer coaches who deliver mindfulness-based mental health interventions for youth anxiety and depression gain psychological benefits themselves, using longitudinal surveys to track coaches' mindfulness, stress resilience, positive and negative affect, and coaching identity before and after coaching.

title: Optimizing Conditions for Tau Protein Crystal Formation for Electron Microscopy Analysis
gloss: Optimizes laboratory conditions for growing crystals of Tau protein fragments, whose misfolding and aggregation are linked to Alzheimer's and other neurodegenerative diseases, so their atomic structure can be studied with microcrystal electron diffraction (MicroED). Crystal formation is assessed with transmission electron microscopy.

title: Between and inter-generational differences in discriminatory experiences among LGBTQ+ individuals assigned female at birth
gloss: Compares experiences of microaggressions and victimization among LGBTQ+ people assigned female at birth across two survey cohorts from 2009 and 2017/2018, examining differences by generation, race/ethnicity, and gender identity, including transgender and gender-diverse participants, through a minority stress framework.

title: Mind and Heart: Perceived Risk and Cognitive Impact of Hypertension Among Refugees
gloss: A mixed-methods study of how Arabic-speaking refugees in San Diego perceive links between hypertension and cognitive decline, and the language, cultural, psychological and structural barriers that affect their blood pressure self-management and care.

title: NQ-13's Therapeutic Potential to Improve Learning and Restore Brain Signaling in Rett Syndrome: Preclinical Evidence from Behavioral and Molecular Assays
gloss: Preclinical drug testing of NQ-13, a novel compound targeting the IGF2R receptor, as a treatment for Rett syndrome, a genetic neurodevelopmental disorder. Behavioral and molecular assays compare it with the existing drug Trofinetide on learning and memory, MeCP2 protein levels, and brain signaling linked to plasticity.

title: The Role of Factor XII in Glioblastoma Progression
gloss: Cancer biology research on how blood clotting factor XII supports cancer stem cells and tumor growth in glioblastoma, a malignant brain tumor, using patient-derived cells and mouse models. It also tests drugs that block factor XII as a possible brain cancer treatment linking coagulation, platelets and tumor immunosuppression.

title: Characterizing the Progression of the interleukin biomarkers in Vivo, for Heart Failure Management
gloss: Studies inflammatory blood biomarkers such as interleukins and cytokines as early, non-invasive indicators of heart failure, tracking inflammation, ECG changes and cardiac injury markers over time in a rat model of chemotherapy (doxorubicin)-induced cardiotoxicity.

title: Positivity Resonance in Youth at Clinical High Risk for Psychosis and Caregivers: Findings from a Dyadic Automated Facial Expressions Analysis Approach
gloss: Studies shared positive emotions (positivity resonance) between youth at clinical high risk for psychosis and their caregivers during conflict and pleasant conversations, using automated facial expression analysis of videorecorded parent-child interactions to examine emotional connection in psychopathology.

title: When Home Becomes a Hospital Room: The Intersection of Caregiver Expectations, Lived Experience, and Child Interactions During Extended Hospital Stays
gloss: A mixed-methods study of parents and caregivers of children with pediatric cancer during extended hospital stays, using surveys and interviews to examine caregiver expectations, stress, guilt, coping, parenting, and parent-child interactions in the hospital, with implications for healthcare communication and family support.

title: Rhetoric Over Rights: How Mississippi Lawmakers Frame Anti-Trans Legislation
gloss: A rhetorical analysis of Mississippi state legislative floor debates on anti-transgender laws, examining how lawmakers on both sides frame their arguments and how transgender people are left out of policymaking on LGBTQ rights in the conservative Deep South.

title: Addressing Safety Measures For Students With Food Allergies In College Dining Halls
gloss: A survey of food allergy accommodations in U.S. college dining halls, examining ingredient labeling, allergy-friendly stations, and access to emergency epinephrine auto-injectors across small, medium, and large universities to assess safety risks for food-allergic students.

title: Peeling, Cracking, and Swelling Patterns of Hydrogels
gloss: An experimental soft matter physics study of how polymer hydrogel discs peel, crack and change shape as they swell with water and dry out through evaporation, examining how cross-linking affects the mechanical behavior of these water-absorbing materials.

title: Synthesizing a Photoactive Molecule with Stability in Water
gloss: Organic synthesis of a water-stable photoactive molecule for building light-responsive hydrogels whose stiffness can be tuned with light, mimicking dynamic tissue mechanics to study how the mechanical environment directs stem cell development and organ formation.

title: Air quality, health, and equity impacts of winter residential wood combustion in the United States
gloss: Uses air quality modeling to estimate how wintertime residential wood burning for home heating contributes to fine particulate (PM2.5) air pollution across the United States, its premature death toll, and how its health burden falls disproportionately on non-White and urban communities.

title: "Story of My Freaking Life" Thematic Integration of Suffering in Life-Story Narratives
gloss: A narrative psychology study of how midlife adults make meaning of suffering in their life stories, using qualitative thematic analysis of life-story interviews to compare how people with higher and lower well-being integrate hardship into their identity.

title: Expanding Knowledge of Music Perception: Analyzing Listeners' Reactions to Justin Timberlake's "Mirrors"
gloss: A music perception study of how listeners segment a pop song into musical ideas, using a segmentation experiment where participants marked new ideas while hearing the audio or watching the music video of Justin Timberlake's "Mirrors," examining how cues like pitch, dynamics, timbre and visual movement signal contrast and repetition.

title: AI in the Newsroom: Use Cases and a Framework for Integration
gloss: A review of how journalists and newsrooms use artificial intelligence tools in news production, from news discovery and reporting to content creation, distribution and audience interaction, organized into a framework of use cases with real-world examples to guide AI adoption in journalism.

title: Evaluating the Accuracy of Preschool Speech and Language Screeners Across Diverse Populations
gloss: Evaluates how accurately common preschool speech and language screening tools identify young children at risk for speech-language disorders across racially, economically and regionally diverse U.S. populations, comparing screener results against clinician judgments to inform equitable early identification and universal screening.

title: Targeting Autophagy: The Neuroprotective Potential of NU-9
gloss: Tests whether the experimental drug NU-9 protects neurons by activating autophagy, the cell's waste-clearing process, using fluorescence and super-resolution microscopy in mouse hippocampal cells. Relevant to clearing toxic protein aggregates such as amyloid-beta in Alzheimer's disease and other neurodegenerative diseases like ALS.

title: A scoping review of sleep disorders in subarachnoid hemorrhage survivors
gloss: A scoping review of published research on sleep problems in survivors of subarachnoid hemorrhage, a type of stroke, mapping how common sleep disorders such as insomnia, sleep apnea and fatigue are, their links to depression and anxiety, and what this means for long-term stroke recovery care.

title: TEAMS (Teamwork-Enhancing Adaptive Machine Synergies)
gloss: Studies whether a large language model AI teammate can improve coordination in multiteam systems, using an experiment in which student groups complete a simulated space exploration task with or without an AI member, measuring task performance, trust between teams, and conflict.

title: Current State of FDA-Approved AI Diagnostic Tools: Regulatory Pathways and Evidence Requirements
gloss: A review of FDA-approved artificial intelligence and machine learning medical diagnostic devices, examining which regulatory approval pathways they used, how much clinical evidence supported them, and how transparent manufacturers were about algorithms and training data. Relevant to health policy, medical device regulation, and AI in healthcare.

title: Lipid membrane properties of peptide-encapsulating biosensors
gloss: A synthetic biology project building a cell-free biosensor that detects peptides using transcriptional regulators, encapsulated in artificial lipid vesicles. It studies how to tune membrane composition to limit permeability, measuring fluorescent signals by microscopy, as a step toward compartmentalized sense-and-respond systems.

title: Are Students' Mental Health Needs Being Met? Evaluating the Effectiveness of Northwestern's Counseling and Psychological Services from the Perspective of Student Users
gloss: A mixed-methods survey and interview study of Northwestern undergraduates' satisfaction with the university's campus counseling and mental health services (CAPS), including how experiences differ by race, gender, sexuality, socioeconomic status and other identities, and how well therapists understand marginalized students.

title: Unconventional Trafficking of a Novel Amphipathic Alpha-Helical Peptide During Drosophila Oogenesis
gloss: Fruit fly developmental cell biology research on how a small peptide made from a short open reading frame is secreted and taken up by cells without a signal sequence, using GFP tagging, transgenic Drosophila and confocal microscopy to track peptide trafficking during egg development and in wing discs.

title: Swing the Stats: The Influence Of Widespread Sports Betting Legalization on Player Performance in Major League Baseball
gloss: A sports data analysis project examining how the legalization of sports betting in the U.S. after 2018 relates to player performance trends in Major League Baseball, using web-scraped player statistics, time-series analysis and statistical testing of offensive and defensive performance.

title: Unveiling Gender Dynamics in Early Kazakhstani Cinema: A Feminist Analysis of KyzZhibek
gloss: A feminist film analysis of the 1972 Soviet-era Kazakh film Kyz-Zhibek, examining how early Kazakhstani cinema portrayed women's roles, arranged marriage and female agency amid nomadic tradition and Soviet modernization, contributing to scholarship on gender representation in Central Asian media.

title: Sedition on Trial: The Bounds of Dissent in Hong Kong Under the National Security Law
gloss: A political science and legal study of how Hong Kong courts have used the colonial-era sedition law under the National Security Law, analyzing judicial reasoning in sedition cases to show how the law restricts free speech and suppresses political dissent.

title: Should Pillar Point be closed to harvesting? Integrating social and ecological perspectives
gloss: Mixed-methods study of community and ecological perspectives on harvesting rules at a California marine protected area tide pool, using questionnaires with local harvesters and fishers and visitor counts to inform marine conservation policy and fishing regulations.

title: Notch1 regulation of Schlemm's canal integrity and endothelial junctional stability
gloss: Studies how the Notch1 signaling gene maintains Schlemm's canal, the eye's drainage vessel that regulates intraocular pressure and is implicated in glaucoma, using knockout mice to examine vessel structure and endothelial cell junction stability.

title: Investigating the Role of Circadian Genes in Intestinal Health
gloss: A mouse study of how genetic disruption of the circadian clock affects gut health, comparing Clock gene mutant mice with normal mice in a chemically induced colitis model and measuring symptoms, gut permeability and intestinal inflammation.

title: Demystifying a Dedication to Artemis Anaitis and Men Tiamou
gloss: A study of an ancient Greek inscription dedicated to the gods Artemis Anaitis and Men in Roman Lydia (western Anatolia), using comparison with other inscriptions to explain its purpose and to shed light on local religion, healing cults and worship of native Anatolian deities in the Roman province.

title: Pollution's Invisible Hand: Air Quality's Role in Neighborhood Sorting by Income in the United States
gloss: An environmental and urban economics study of how air pollution affects where people of different incomes choose to live in the United States, and how this residential sorting changes neighborhood income, housing values and economic opportunity.

title: Educators' Beliefs About Students' Background Specific Strengths As a Means to Foster Motivation and Academic Success
gloss: A psychology study of how middle school students' perceptions that their teachers value the strengths they bring from their backgrounds relate to identity-based motivation, grades, and racial disparities in academic achievement, with attention to Black, Latinx, and Indigenous students and educational equity.

title: Hypnagogic Thoughts and Creativity
gloss: A cognitive neuroscience study of whether thoughts during hypnagogia, the drowsy transition between wakefulness and sleep, boost creativity and problem solving. It uses EEG sleep monitoring during rest breaks and compares the results with mind wandering while awake.

title: Beyond Risk: The Changing Influences of Social and Physical Contexts on theHealthPromoting Behaviors of Undergraduate Students
gloss: A sociology study using surveys and interviews to examine how parents, friends, roommates, and the college environment shape undergraduate students' health-promoting behaviors such as eating and exercise, and how time pressures of college life affect student health.

title: Me vs We: Optimal Distinctiveness and Attachment Style in Romantic Relationships
gloss: A social psychology study of how attachment style (anxious or avoidant) shapes how much closeness versus independence people want in romantic relationships, applying optimal distinctiveness theory through surveys and experiments with partnered adults and linking ideal-versus-actual closeness to relationship satisfaction.

title: Investigating the role of FBN-1 in Ovarian Aging
gloss: Reproductive biology research on ovarian aging and female fertility decline, studying whether loss of the extracellular matrix protein fibrillin-1 in aging mouse and human ovaries disrupts elastic fibers and drives TGF-beta signaling and ovarian fibrosis.

title: Developing a New Biomaterial to Break Down Proteins Linked to Injury and Disease
gloss: Develops a peptide amphiphile biomaterial that forms micelles carrying antibodies and sugar tags to deliver disease-related proteins, such as Alzheimer's amyloid-beta, into cell lysosomes for degradation, as a potential therapy for neurodegenerative and other diseases.

title: Greener Energy Requires Greener Batteries: Design and Evaluation of the Mixed-Metal Pyrochlore as a Battery Cathode
gloss: Materials chemistry research on sustainable lithium-ion battery cathodes made from earth-abundant elements, synthesizing an iron fluoride pyrochlore with partial manganese substitution and characterizing it to see whether it improves charge retention and voltage for grid-scale green energy storage.

title: After the Highland Park Mass Shooting: Impacts on Gun-Ideology, Identity, and Community
gloss: An interview study of how the 2022 Highland Park, Illinois mass shooting affected residents' sense of community, identity, gun ownership, and attitudes toward gun control. Uses qualitative interviews to understand the aftermath of gun violence on a community.

title: Stereotyping and Racial Perception of Multiracial Individuals
gloss: A social psychology experiment on how people racially categorize multiracial individuals, testing whether exposure to positive or negative racial stereotypes shapes those perceptions. It relates stereotyping to identity denial experienced by multiracial people.

title: Equalizer No More: Chinese, Black, and Choctaw Education in The Age of Separate and Unequal Policies
gloss: An interdisciplinary Asian American Studies thesis comparing the schooling of Chinese, Black, and Indigenous (Choctaw) children in the segregated U.S. South, using legal history and education policy to examine racialization, antiblackness, settler colonialism, and the myth of education as the great equalizer.

title: Building or Breaking Trust: The Effectiveness of Chicago Community Policing Programs on Building LGBTQ+ Trust
gloss: Evaluates whether the Chicago Police Department's LGBTQ+ Liaison Program, a community policing effort under the federal consent decree, builds LGBTQ+ community trust in police. Uses interviews with community stakeholders and ethnographic observation of police beat meetings.

title: Order and Comprehension Effects in Death Penalty Jurors' Decision-Making
gloss: A psychology and law study of how mock jurors decide death penalty sentences, testing whether the order of mitigating and aggravating evidence, understanding of jury instructions, and juror demographics such as gender and age influence choices between death and life in prison.

title: The Impact of Systemic Inflammation and Cholinergic Antagonism on Slow Wave Activity in Cortical Areas
gloss: A neuroscience study of delirium in mice, using widefield calcium imaging to measure how systemic inflammation (lipopolysaccharide) and the anticholinergic drug scopolamine change slow wave brain activity across different regions of the cortex.

title: Making Cool Water: Evaporative Cooling in Caribbean Coarse Earthenware
gloss: An experimental archaeology study of how porous Caribbean earthenware water jars (goglets), like those used on 18th- and 19th-century sugar plantations, cool stored water through evaporation, and what this reveals about historical pottery use and material choice.

title: Scrolling Into the Future: Social Media and Gen Z Men's Education and Career Pathways
gloss: A qualitative sociology study using interviews with young Gen Z men to examine how social media shapes their career aspirations and education choices, including perceptions of college, trades and alternative credentials, and entrepreneurship, alongside masculinity and status expectations of success.

title: Synthesis of MAP2K4/7 Inhibitors: Overcoming Drug Resistance in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
gloss: Medicinal chemistry project designing and synthesizing small-molecule inhibitors of the kinases MAP2K4/7 to overcome drug resistance in pancreatic cancer. Blocking this MAPK signaling branch aims to stop feedback reactivation of KRAS and restore the effectiveness of KRAS-targeted cancer therapies.

title: Investigating Drug-Based Strategies to Improve Lysosomal Function in CLN7 Neuropediatric Batten Disease
gloss: Lab research on CLN7 Batten disease, a childhood neurodegenerative lysosomal storage disorder, examining why the lysosomal protein CLN5 is lost in cells lacking MFSD8 and testing whether drugs that inhibit lysosomal proteases can restore lysosomal function as a treatment strategy.

title: Symbolic Play Engagement in Early Childhood: The Extent to Which Toy and Non-Toy Object Availability Explains Differences in Pretend Play
gloss: A child development study of pretend (symbolic) play in young children, examining how the availability of toys and everyday non-toy objects at home shapes their play. It uses coded home videos of mother-child play interactions from linguistically and culturally diverse families.

title: Ingredients of Our Black Hole's Diet: Correlating Different Gas Phases in the Center of the Milky Way
gloss: Studies how gas feeds or is pushed away from Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way, by mapping cold molecular and hot ionized gas with ALMA radio telescope data and machine learning to identify structures tied to black hole feeding and feedback.

title: Foreign Domestic Workers in Hong Kong: A Study of the Impacts of Low-Skill Immigrants on Native Female Labour Decisions
gloss: An economics study of how foreign domestic workers and low-skill immigration affect native women's employment and labor supply, using Hong Kong census data and US survey data to examine gender, immigration policy and work decisions.

title: "Why don't fidget toys work?": Embodied artifacts in a MS summer camp.
gloss: Ethnographic education research on how movement and the body relate to focus and learning in a STEAM and storytelling summer camp for middle schoolers of color, using field notes, video, and educator interviews to inform curriculum redesign.

title: Characterizing Peptoids as an Alternative Nanoparticle Stealth Coating
gloss: Compares peptoid polymers with standard PEG linkers for attaching folic acid to gold nanoparticles, testing how linker architecture affects nanoparticle stability and targeting of breast cancer cells for targeted drug delivery and cancer nanomedicine.

title: Evaluating Reliance on Misinformation for Video Stimuli
gloss: A cognitive psychology experiment testing whether the continued influence effect, people's ongoing reliance on retracted misinformation, occurs with video rather than text, using fictional news broadcasts and testing whether an alternative explanation reduces reliance on the corrected claim.

title: Optimization of an inducible genetic strategy to study olfactory monoallelic expression
gloss: Mouse neuroscience project optimizing a tamoxifen-inducible Cre genetic system to control gene activity in developing olfactory sensory neurons, as groundwork for studying how each smell-detecting neuron chooses to express only one odorant receptor gene.

title: Early Adversity, Meaning-Making, and the Construction of Narrative Identity among Exceptionally Generative Latina Leaders
gloss: A qualitative psychology study of how Latina activists and community organizers make meaning of early adversity and trauma in their life stories, using autobiographical interviews to examine narrative identity, generativity, and how suffering sustains commitment to advocacy and social justice work.

title: Earth System History Repeats Itself: Contextualizing our Current Situation Through Records of Ancient Volcanism and Acidification
gloss: Geochemistry study of ancient ocean acidification and volcanism during Ocean Anoxic Event 2, about 94 million years ago, using calcium, carbon and osmium isotope analysis of rocks from two sites to understand past climate change and inform projections of modern, carbon-emission-driven ocean acidification.

title: Rupture Instabilities of Thin Colloidal Films
gloss: Experimental fluid dynamics study of how thin liquid films containing suspended colloidal particles rupture, using high-speed video to examine how film thickness, particle concentration, and particle shape (rods or spheres) affect non-Newtonian rupture instabilities and rupture speed.

title: Liposomal Spherical Nucleic Acid (LSNA) for the Treatment of Inflammation
gloss: Develops liposome-based spherical nucleic acid nanoparticles to deliver inhibitory DNA oligonucleotides that block immune receptor activation, as an alternative or complement to steroids for treating chronic inflammatory diseases. Tests the nanoparticles' anti-inflammatory effects in cell culture.

title: Language Deprivation from Structural Violence: Trauma, LDS, and Implications
gloss: A qualitative synthesis of historical, policy, and research literature arguing that trauma and mental health harms among deaf people stem from structural language deprivation rather than deafness itself, examining Language Deprivation Syndrome and calling for early sign language access and reforms in deaf education and healthcare.

title: shRNA-Mediated Knockdown of SPTLC3 Impairs Epidermal Differentiation and Filaggrin Expression in 3D Skin Organoid Models
gloss: Eczema (atopic dermatitis) skin barrier research testing how reducing the ceramide-making gene SPTLC3 in human keratinocytes affects skin development and filaggrin levels, using shRNA gene knockdown in lab-grown 3D skin organoids.

title: Gender-Based Personality Differences in Early-Stage Entrepreneurs
gloss: A psychology study of entrepreneur personality that uses personality assessments to compare early-stage entrepreneurs with successful founders and to examine gender differences among early-stage entrepreneurs in traits such as ambition, risk-taking, empathy, neuroticism, and leadership.

title: The Role of Serine Palmitolyltransferase Single Small Unit B in the Skin Barrier
gloss: Studies how the protein SPTSSB, which helps produce long-chain ceramide fats, affects the skin barrier and eczema (atopic dermatitis). Uses lab-grown 3D human skin models with reduced SPTSSB to examine effects on skin development, pointing to a potential eczema treatment target.

title: Neural Correlates of Spectral and Temporal Perceptual Strategies in Music-in-Noise Performance
gloss: An auditory neuroscience study of how people hear music in background noise, linking individual listening strategies (relying on pitch versus rhythm or visual cues) to differences in how the brain encodes sound, measured with EEG frequency-following responses in young adults.

title: Interrupted! Using a Virtual Museum Video Game to Study Task-Switching
gloss: Cognitive psychology study using a virtual museum video game to measure task-switching and cognitive flexibility under naturalistic conditions, examining how working memory distractions disrupt episodic memory, with normative data from healthy participants and planned comparison to epilepsy patients undergoing intracranial EEG.

title: Beyond the Cytoskeleton: Vimentin as a Regulator of Chemotherapy Resistance in Glioblastoma
gloss: Cancer biology research on glioblastoma, an aggressive brain tumor, examining how the protein vimentin contributes to chemotherapy (temozolomide) resistance by binding DNA and regulating genes in the nucleus. Uses patient-derived tumor cell lines, protein imaging, and genomic mapping to identify drug-resistance pathways and potential therapeutic targets.

title: Group Singing as Treatment for Children's Wellness
gloss: Music and mental health research on whether weekly group singing, with breathing and stretching exercises, improves wellbeing in children aged 8-12 after the Covid-19 pandemic, using surveys, heart rate variability data and interviews.

title: Living, Working, and Playing: Asian American Environmental Justice Before the Movement
gloss: A history paper applying the environmental justice framework to Asian American activism and community organizing before the 1991 environmental justice movement, examining cases in San Francisco and Hawai'i to challenge the model minority myth of Asian American political passivity.

title: Isolating the Utility of Planning Against a Dynamic Threat in Naturalistic DecisionMaking
gloss: Neuroscience study of decision-making and planning in mice, testing whether a mobile robotic predator in an open, obstacle-free arena is enough to disrupt habitual navigation and trigger planning-like escape and reward-seeking behavior, using high-resolution tracking of mouse movement.

title: Exploring fathers' health behavior motivations to leverage healthcare engagement in the perinatal period: A qualitative study
gloss: A qualitative interview study of new fathers and their partners exploring what motivates fathers' health behaviors around pregnancy and childbirth, and how the perinatal period could be used to engage men with their own preventive healthcare and primary care.

title: Effects of Independence and Interdependence Priming on Big Five Personality Trait Reporting
gloss: A psychology experiment testing whether priming independent versus interdependent self-construal changes how people report their Big Five personality traits, and whether cultural self-construal differences predict personality self-reports.

title: Internal Fact-Checking and the Crisis of Trust in News Mediaa
gloss: A journalism thesis on fact-checking and declining public trust in American news media, comparing external political fact-checking with internal pre-publication verification through practitioner interviews and media psychology research, and arguing that newsrooms should prioritize internal fact-checking.

title: Altered Foodways: The Impact of Colonialism on PCOS Prevalence in the Andes
gloss: A systematic literature review on how Spanish colonialism changed diets and food systems among Indigenous and mestizo Andean peoples, and how the shift toward processed, high-carbohydrate foods relates to high rates of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a reproductive and metabolic disorder.

title: Structural and Functional Insights into ProU Regulation: Investigating CBS-Mediated Inhibition in Yersinia pestis
gloss: Structural biology study of how bacteria survive osmotic stress, using X-ray crystallography to determine the structure of the regulatory CBS domain of ProU, an ABC transporter that imports osmoprotectants in the plague bacterium Yersinia pestis, to understand transporter regulation and inform new antibacterial targets.

title: Using arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) as indicators of belowground responses to urban river corridor restoration in Chicago
gloss: Studies how soil arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi and soil properties change along a prairie restoration gradient in Chicago River corridor sites, using fungal abundance as an indicator of belowground ecosystem recovery in urban ecological restoration.

title: Altered Kinetics and Voltage Dependence of Activation in a Pathogenic KCNH1 Potassium Channel Variant
gloss: Electrophysiology study of how a recurrent disease-causing mutation in the KCNH1 potassium channel gene changes channel opening and voltage sensitivity, using patch clamp recordings in cultured cells. Relates ion channel dysfunction to epilepsy and the neurodevelopmental disorders Temple-Baraitser and Zimmermann-Laband syndromes.

title: Psychological States and Responses to Constructive Friendship Criticism: Comparing Self-Affirmation, Felt Security, and Ego-Threat
gloss: A social psychology experiment on how people respond to constructive criticism from close friends, testing whether self-affirmation, felt security, or ego-threat changes defensiveness, trust and receptiveness to feedback in friendships.

title: Poetic Medicine: Black Feminist Poetics of Cancer and HIV/AIDS
gloss: A literary study of Black women's poetry and creative nonfiction about illness, comparing writing on cancer and HIV/AIDS to show how poetry serves as personal and collective healing and captures experiences of illness that medical systems overlook, with the aim of broadening public health practice.

title: Investigating the Effect of Linguistic Labeling on Object Categorization and Memory in 7 and 12-Month-Olds: Evidence from a "Peek-a-Boo" Occlusion Task
gloss: Infant cognitive development study testing whether hearing objects named with distinct made-up words helps 7- and 12-month-old babies categorize and remember objects, using a peek-a-boo occlusion task and looking-time measures of surprise.

title: How Bacteria Tell Time: Mathematical Models of the Cyanobacterial Circadian Clock
gloss: Mathematical modeling of the circadian clock in cyanobacteria, comparing traditional differential equation models with stochastic simulations that add biological noise to test how sensitive this biochemical timekeeping system is to random fluctuations.

title: Knockdown of Clock in Ventral Tegmental Area Dopamine Neurons Influences BipolarLike Behaviors and Sleep Deprivation Responses in Mice
gloss: Mouse neuroscience study of how knocking down the circadian clock gene Clock in ventral tegmental area dopamine neurons early in life affects bipolar disorder-like mania, anxiety and depression behaviors, and responses to sleep deprivation, linking circadian rhythm disruption and dopamine circuits to mood disorders.

title: Probabilistic Neural Operator for Dynamical Systems Under Uncertainty
gloss: Develops a machine learning method using neural operators to predict how dynamical systems evolve over time while quantifying uncertainty, combining quantile regression and Bayesian ideas to produce confidence intervals that account for noisy data and model limitations, with comparisons to existing uncertainty estimation methods.

title: Clean Conscience: Exploring College Students' Enactment of Environmental Beliefs Through Domestic Labor
gloss: A sociology study using in-depth interviews with Northwestern undergraduates to examine how gender shapes college students' environmental beliefs and pro-environmental behavior, including household and domestic labor, and whether the feminization of environmental action seen in adults persists on campus.

title: The King and Queen of Rock: Little Richard, Religion, and the Stipulations of Black Queer Fame
gloss: A historical study of rock and roll pioneer Little Richard examining how race, queer sexuality, religion, and fame shaped his shifting public identity, using biographies, interviews, and scholarship on Black queerness, race theory, and music history.

title: Cardiac Synchrony in Co-Rumination Dyads: Using EKG to Study Interpersonal Dysfunction in Depression
gloss: Psychology research on depression and social relationships, using EKG heart rate and heart rate variability data to test whether friends who co-ruminate (excessively discuss problems and negative emotions) show physiological cardiac synchrony during conversation, as a marker of interpersonal dysfunction.

title: Decoding Decisions: Folk Theories of Urgent Care Triage Algorithms from Koreatown (K-Town), Los Angeles
gloss: Qualitative study of how low-income patients and families in Koreatown, Los Angeles form informal folk theories about urgent care triage and algorithmic bias in healthcare, using interviews and autoethnography to show how these perceptions shape decisions about seeking or leaving care.

title: Post-Colonial Community Perspectives on Cultural Heritage and Archaeology in Corozal, Belize
gloss: An anthropology study of how community members in Corozal, Belize perceive and engage with cultural heritage and archaeology in a post-colonial context, using photo-prompted community discussions to examine heritage management, who benefits from defining heritage sites, and relationships between locals and archaeologists.

title: HANDFUL: Dexterous Multi-Step Robot Manipulation with Resource Awareness
gloss: A machine learning framework and simulation benchmark for multi-step manipulation with dexterous robot hands, teaching robots to grasp objects with few fingers so the remaining fingers stay free for follow-up tasks like pushing, pulling a drawer, pressing a button or twisting a knob, tested on a real robot hand.

title: My Tutor Bot: Integrating Large Language Models into Intelligent Tutoring Systems for Fundamental Programming
gloss: Builds and evaluates an AI chatbot tutor powered by a large language model for an introductory computer science programming course, studying how AI tutoring affects student learning, engagement and educational equity in STEM using chat logs, interviews and surveys.

title: Antisemitism and Anti-Zionism: A Case Study on Jewish Student perspectives at Northwestern University
gloss: An interview-based sociology thesis on how Jewish undergraduates at Northwestern University understand the relationship between anti-Zionism and antisemitism, examining their experiences of campus climate, political discourse, and identity amid campus protests and national scrutiny.

title: Inafa'maolek Archaeologies: CHamoru heritage resurgence amidst U.S. militarization on Guahan (Guam)
gloss: An ethnographic study of Indigenous CHamoru archaeologists and historic preservationists on Guam who protect cultural heritage amid U.S. military build-up. It examines how they bring Indigenous knowledge into cultural resource management and use archaeology for decolonial heritage education and sovereignty.
